Borrowing money to invest

oldEnglishRecords.question: What is portfolio 'rebalancing'?

Periodically adjusting holdings back to your target mix
Adding only the best-performing stock
Checking your balance every day

englishRecords.question: The same weighted basket costs PLN 1,000, then PLN 1,050. What does this illustration show?

answers.text: Every price must rise by 5%
Basket prices rise 5%; the same cash buys less
All household costs rise by exactly 5%
One higher price alone proves general inflation

englishRecords.successMessage: The basket rises 5%; each price and household can differ. +25 local points.
englishRecords.retryMessage: Inflation concerns a broad weighted basket, not one price. Here (1,050 ÷ 1,000 − 1) × 100% = 5%; the same cash buys less of that basket. Different households have different spending baskets.

englishRecords.question: In this example you choose 3 months at PLN 2,000 of essential costs (required debt minimums included once). What is the goal with constant costs?
englishRecords.successMessage: Chosen goal: 3 × 2,000 = PLN 6,000. An example, not a required threshold. +25 local points.
englishRecords.retryMessage: 3 × PLN 2,000 = PLN 6,000 under the stated constant costs, with debt minimums already included once. Reserve size depends on circumstances; 3–6 months can be an indicative choice without guaranteed protection. This gives no completion date or transfer obligation.

englishRecords.question: Which transfer is safe when income varies?

answers.text: Save a fixed amount even if bills are unpaid
Borrow money to keep saving every month
Choose an affordable amount after essentials and minimum payments
Transfer all income before checking upcoming bills

englishRecords.successMessage: An optional transfer uses affordable surplus after essentials and required minimum payments. +25 local points.
englishRecords.retryMessage: Reserve essentials and required minimum payments first. Then choose an optional transfer from available surplus. Recheck its amount and timing when income varies; pause when there is no surplus.

englishRecords.question: Hypothetical loan: a 3% reference rate + a 2 percentage-point margin. At the contractual reset the reference rises to 4%; the margin is unchanged. What is the new rate?
englishRecords.successMessage: 4% + 2 percentage points = 6% at the contractual reset. +25 local points.
englishRecords.retryMessage: The new reference replaces the old: 4% + the unchanged 2 percentage-point margin = 6%. The contract sets the timing; a central-bank decision alone does not instantly change every installment. A rate can be fixed or periodically fixed. Check the agreed period and the subsequent contractual terms when it ends; this does not freeze every fee.

englishRecords.question: What is 'net worth'?

answers.text: Your monthly salary after tax
Total assets minus total liabilities
How much cash you have in your wallet
Your credit score

englishRecords.successMessage: Net worth = assets minus liabilities at the same date. It describes a financial position, not your value as a person or whether cash is available for this month's bills. +25 points!
englishRecords.retryMessage: Net worth is assets minus liabilities at the same date. Income is a flow; cash and credit scores are different measures. Net worth alone does not describe liquidity or your value as a person.

englishRecords.question: What is 'lifestyle inflation'?

answers.text: Government increasing minimum wage
Prices rising faster than salaries
Choosing more discretionary spending as your income rises
Inflating your lifestyle on your resume

englishRecords.successMessage: Lifestyle inflation concerns choices about a higher standard of living. Higher prices or necessary costs are different. If there is a surplus after needs and commitments, you can choose to save part of it. +25 points!
englishRecords.retryMessage: Lifestyle inflation is a voluntary rise in discretionary spending as income grows. It is different from price inflation or necessary expenses, and it does not mean every raise is fully spent.

englishRecords.question: What does 'pay yourself first' mean?

answers.text: Spend on yourself before paying bills
Plan affordable savings after reserving money for essentials and required minimum payments
Increase your own salary first
Buy luxury items before groceries

englishRecords.successMessage: Plan savings from available surplus after protecting essentials and required minimum payments. With irregular income, review each payment; with no surplus, skip the transfer. +20 points!
englishRecords.retryMessage: First reserve money for essentials and required minimum payments, then choose savings from available surplus before discretionary spending. A transfer is optional; no surplus means no transfer, without blame.

englishRecords.question: With PLN 4,000 take-home income, what is the illustrative 20% bucket?

answers.text: PLN 800

englishRecords.successMessage: 20% of PLN 4,000 is PLN 800. The percentages are a flexible guide. +25 local points.
englishRecords.retryMessage: 4,000 × 20% = PLN 800. In this example, required minimum debt payments are included once in needs; the 20% bucket is savings and extra debt repayment. This is our illustration convention, not a compulsory split.

englishRecords.question: Which checklist is most complete when comparing savings accounts in Poland?

answers.text: Only the advertised interest rate
Rates and conditions, fees, access, and deposit protection
Whether the account guarantees an inflation-beating return
Whether your deposit is automatically invested in stocks

englishRecords.successMessage: Compare actual conditions and costs, not just the advertised rate. +20 local points.
englishRecords.retryMessage: Check the rate and its duration, qualifying conditions, fees, withdrawal access, and the applicable deposit guarantee scheme. A deposit account is not a stock investment; inflation can still reduce purchasing power.

englishRecords.question: You invest PLN 100 twice, at PLN 10 then PLN 20 per unit. What do you buy?

answers.text: 10 units both times
5 units then 10 units
10 units then 5 units

englishRecords.retryMessage: ISA (UK), NISA (Japan) and IKE (Poland) are tax-advantaged accounts that shelter investment gains.

englishRecords.question: What inflation target does India's central bank (RBI) aim for?

answers.text: 4% with a ±2 percentage point tolerance band
It has no target

englishRecords.successMessage: The RBI targets 4% inflation with a ±2pp band (2–6%), retained through 2026–2031. +25 tokens!
englishRecords.retryMessage: India's RBI targets 4% inflation with a tolerance band of ±2 percentage points (2–6%).

allChallengeRecords.question: How should 50/30/20 be understood as a flexible guide for take-home income?

answers.text: 50% savings, 30% needs, 20% wants
50% needs, 30% wants, 20% savings and debt payments
Always save 20%, even at the expense of essential bills
Borrow in order to save exactly 20%

allChallengeRecords.explanation: 50/30/20 is an illustrative split of take-home income that can be adapted. First protect essential needs and required minimum repayments; do not count the same payment twice. Adjust amounts when income varies. Without a surplus, do not force 20% saving.

allChallengeRecords.question: Model: PLN 1,000, a constant hypothetical 5% a year, annual compounding, interest retained. No contributions, withdrawals, fees or tax; inflation ignored. Nominal balance after 2 years?
allChallengeRecords.explanation: Compounding adds interest on retained earlier interest. In the model, 1,000 × 1.05 × 1.05 = PLN 1,102.50. The positive result depends on the assumed 5%, not time alone. This is a hypothetical calculation, with no guarantee of actual gains; investments can lose value.

allChallengeRecords.question: Which statement describes diversification and its limit?

answers.text: Everything in one strong company
Different assets can reduce concentration; losses remain possible
One bond removes every risk
Frequent trades guarantee protection from a decline

allChallengeRecords.explanation: Diversification spreads exposure across different assets and can reduce concentration risk. It does not remove market risk or guarantee avoiding losses. Different fund names may hide similar holdings; check holdings, risk and costs. No purchase is required.

allChallengeRecords.question: How does a debt avalanche work once essentials and all required minimum repayments are covered?

answers.text: Finances every extra payment with a new loan
Always starts with the smallest balance
Puts an available extra payment toward the highest-rate debt
Skips required payments on other debts

allChallengeRecords.explanation: An avalanche puts available extra money toward the highest rate after essentials and every debt minimum. With fixed rates and no extra fees, it can reduce interest. Check fees and consequences of arrears; without a surplus, do not force an extra payment. It does not guarantee the lowest total cost under all conditions.

allChallengeRecords.question: Hypothetical: nominal return +2% and inflation 5% over the same year, no fees or tax. What is the rounded real return?

answers.text: About −2.86%

allChallengeRecords.explanation: The exact relation is (1.02 ÷1.05 −1) × 100% ≈ −2.86%. Subtracting 2% −5% =−3% is an approximation. Initial PLN 1,000 becomes nominal PLN 1,020, or about PLN 971.43 in initial prices. The model uses the same year and no fees or tax; it is not a current offer.

allChallengeRecords.question: Which statement about funds is correct?

answers.text: Every ETF always tracks an index
An index fund tracks an index; an ETF can be indexed or active
Every index fund is the cheapest
Every ETF guarantees beating the market

allChallengeRecords.explanation: An index fund aims to track an index. An ETF is an exchange-traded fund structure; it can be indexed or active. Neither label guarantees low costs, beating the market or avoiding losses. Check the objective, holdings, risk and all costs. You do not have to invest.

allChallengeRecords.question: Which statement describes DCA?

answers.text: Investing the whole amount only at the lowest price
Selling everything after every decline
An equal amount at regular intervals, regardless of price
Converting savings into dollars

allChallengeRecords.explanation: DCA uses an equal amount at regular intervals; a lower price buys more units. It guarantees neither profit nor protection from loss and does not automatically remove emotions. With no fees or tax: PLN 100 at 10 and PLN 100 at 20 buys 15 units. At 8 they are worth PLN 120 versus PLN 200 contributed. Contributions are optional, after essentials and required minimum repayments.

allChallengeRecords.question: Rule 72: a hypothetical constant positive 8% nominal annual rate, annual compounding, no contributions, withdrawals, fees or tax; inflation ignored. What doubling-time estimate does the rule give?

answers.text: About 6 years
About 9 years
About 72 years
Exactly 9 years for every investment

allChallengeRecords.explanation: 72 ÷8 ≈ 9 years is an approximation, not an exact date. In the model, 1,000 × 1.08⁹ ≈ PLN 1,999.00; after 10 annual credits it exceeds PLN 2,000. A constant positive 8% is an assumption, not a forecast. Actual rates may change and investments can lose value. This nominal model excludes cash flows, fees, tax and inflation.

allChallengeRecords.question: What is an ETF?

answers.text: A deposit guaranteeing a stated interest payment
An electronic transfer fee
An exchange-traded fund, indexed or actively managed
A government emergency reserve

allChallengeRecords.explanation: An ETF is an exchange-traded fund. It may track an index or be actively managed. Diversification depends on actual holdings; a narrow-sector fund can be concentrated. The label guarantees neither low costs nor freedom from loss. Check objectives, holdings, risks and costs; no purchase is required.

allChallengeRecords.question: Which choice does NOT fit the purpose of an emergency reserve?

answers.text: Ready access for an unexpected expense
A situation-based goal and small achievable start
High-risk stocks solely for maximum growth
Keeping the reserve separate from everyday spending

allChallengeRecords.explanation: A reserve aims to make funds accessible for unexpected needs with limited risk, rather than maximize returns. Keep it separate from everyday spending. Size depends on circumstances;3–6 months is an optional guide, not a duty or guarantee. Start voluntarily after essentials and required minimum repayments; without a surplus, pause contributions.

allChallengeRecords.question: What generally happens to an existing fixed-coupon bond’s secondary-market price when comparable market yields rise and all other conditions stay equal?

answers.text: The price rises
The price falls
The price always equals face value
The price must double

allChallengeRecords.explanation: With fixed cash flows and all else equal, a higher market yield means a lower secondary-market price. The agreed coupon does not rise automatically. A sale price before maturity differs from contractual payments. Repayment also depends on the issuer’s ability to pay; default and liquidity risk remain.

allChallengeRecords.question: Hypothetically, monthly income rises by PLN 200 and discretionary spending by PLN 180; essentials and required minimum repayments are unchanged. How much does the surplus rise?

answers.text: PLN 200
PLN 180
PLN 20
It can never change

allChallengeRecords.explanation: 200 − 180 = PLN 20 of extra monthly surplus. Discretionary spending rising with income illustrates lifestyle inflation, distinct from rising prices and necessary costs. Not every pay rise must be saved. Adapt the plan to essentials, required minimum repayments, goals and variable income; this is not a judgment of the person.

allChallengeRecords.question: What is the main purpose of long-term retirement planning?

answers.text: Guaranteed doubling of every balance
Preparing resources for future needs when work changes or ends
Replacing an emergency reserve with a risky investment
A certain tax benefit for every payment and every account

allChallengeRecords.explanation: Planning helps prepare resources for future needs but guarantees neither full income replacement nor profit. A retirement goal alone does not give every account a tax benefit. Essentials, required minimum repayments and reserves come before optional investment. Adjust or pause contributions when income varies.

allChallengeRecords.question: Hypothetically on a given date: assets PLN 50,000 and liabilities PLN 20,000. What is net worth?

answers.text: Monthly salary

allChallengeRecords.explanation: Net worth =assets −liabilities:50,000 − 20,000 = PLN 30,000 on that date. It is a wealth snapshot, not monthly income and expense flows or available cash. It does not define overall financial well-being or a person’s worth. Valuations and liabilities may change.

allChallengeRecords.question: Hypothetical month: PLN 100 remains after essentials and required repayments; no other funds are available. A new payment is PLN 150. What does the budget show?

answers.text: Knowing compound interest covers the missing PLN 50
An unconfirmed pay rise guarantees repayment
PLN 50 is missing; check costs and affordability before deciding
Borrow PLN 50 and assume the budget is unchanged

allChallengeRecords.explanation: 100 − 150 = −PLN 50. Essentials and existing required repayments have already been deducted once in this example. Knowing compound interest alone does not provide income or ensure repayment. Before a new commitment, check full costs, dates and a realistic budget; allow for fluctuations with variable income. Another loan does not prove that this payment is covered by the stated budget.

allChallengeRecords.question: Which checklist is most complete when comparing surveys of trust in financial institutions?

answers.text: Only the publication headline
Only the year, without sample information
The number of likes on the publication
Year, sample, question wording and measurement method

allChallengeRecords.explanation: Check who was surveyed, when, what was asked and how the result was calculated. Different questions or samples limit comparability. Declared trust is not a certificate that a particular institution is safe or proof of an effect on wealth.

allChallengeRecords.question: Exercise: a made-up 0–21-point scale gives a score of 13. What does the gap to the maximum mean?

answers.text: 8 lost opportunities for profit
8 points under the chosen scoring key, not a wealth diagnosis
8 months without money
8 people without an account

allChallengeRecords.explanation: 21 − 13 = 8 points in this exercise. This made-up scale is not the current OECD scale; points are not a count of questions. Points alone prove neither behaviour, debt, resilience nor the causes of difficulties. Survey results need a year, sample, questions and scoring key; measurement versions can differ.

allChallengeRecords.question: Exercise: this month, PLN 50 remains after essential needs and required minimum repayments. Which step is voluntary and fits within that amount?

answers.text: Borrow PLN 100 to make a compulsory saving of 100
Skip a required repayment
Choose PLN 10 for a reserve and leave PLN 40
Assume a small transfer will remove all stress

allChallengeRecords.explanation: 50 − 10 = PLN 40 in the same month; essentials and required repayments were already counted once. A small step is an option, not a duty or a guarantee of no stress. Without a surplus, pause contributions; do not borrow to save. When income varies, return to the plan and adjust the amount.

allChallengeRecords.question: Which Polish term means money set aside for unexpected, unplanned expenses?

answers.text: Pay for current work
Poduszka finansowa (emergency reserve)
A required loan to fund savings
A certain investment profit

allChallengeRecords.explanation: An emergency reserve is kept separately for unexpected expenses. Adapt the goal to your circumstances; a small start is voluntary, with no single mandatory threshold. First protect essential needs and required minimum repayments; without a surplus, pause contributions. Check access and risk; a reserve cannot automatically cover every event.

allChallengeRecords.question: What do attitudes towards money describe in a survey?

answers.text: The number of products owned
Income level and wealth
Stated views on spending, saving and the future
Guaranteed repayment capacity

allChallengeRecords.explanation: These are stated views, such as spending today versus saving for the future. They are not a knowledge test or a full measure of behaviour or financial circumstances. Stated views alone prove neither the cause of difficulties nor a future outcome. Income and essential costs also shape possibilities; avoid judging the person.

en.question: The same weighted basket costs PLN 1,000, then PLN 1,050. What does this illustration show?

answers.text: Every price must rise by 5%
Basket prices rise 5%; the same cash buys less
All household costs rise by exactly 5%
One higher price alone proves general inflation

en.explanation: Inflation concerns a broad weighted basket, not one price. Here (1,050 ÷ 1,000 − 1) × 100% = 5%; the same cash buys less of that basket. Different households have different spending baskets.

en.question: In this example you choose 3 months at PLN 2,000 of essential costs (required debt minimums included once). What is the goal with constant costs?
en.explanation: 3 × PLN 2,000 = PLN 6,000 under the stated constant costs, with debt minimums already included once. Reserve size depends on circumstances; 3–6 months can be an indicative choice without guaranteed protection. This gives no completion date or transfer obligation.

en.question: Which transfer is safe when income varies?

answers.text: Save a fixed amount even if bills are unpaid
Borrow money to keep saving every month
Choose an affordable amount after essentials and minimum payments
Transfer all income before checking upcoming bills

en.explanation: Reserve essentials and required minimum payments first. Then choose an optional transfer from available surplus. Recheck its amount and timing when income varies; pause when there is no surplus.

en.question: Hypothetical loan: a 3% reference rate + a 2 percentage-point margin. At the contractual reset the reference rises to 4%; the margin is unchanged. What is the new rate?
en.explanation: The new reference replaces the old: 4% + the unchanged 2 percentage-point margin = 6%. The contract sets the timing; a central-bank decision alone does not instantly change every installment. A rate can be fixed or periodically fixed. Check the agreed period and the subsequent contractual terms when it ends; this does not freeze every fee.

en.question: What is 'net worth'?

answers.text: Your monthly salary after tax
Total assets minus total liabilities
How much cash you have in your wallet
Your credit score

en.explanation: Net worth is assets minus liabilities at the same date. Income is a flow; cash and credit scores are different measures. Net worth alone does not describe liquidity or your value as a person.

en.question: What is 'lifestyle inflation'?

answers.text: Government increasing minimum wage
Prices rising faster than salaries
Choosing more discretionary spending as your income rises
Inflating your lifestyle on your resume

en.explanation: Lifestyle inflation is a voluntary rise in discretionary spending as income grows. It is different from price inflation or necessary expenses, and it does not mean every raise is fully spent.

en.question: What does 'pay yourself first' mean?

answers.text: Spend on yourself before paying bills
Plan affordable savings after reserving money for essentials and required minimum payments
Increase your own salary first
Buy luxury items before groceries

en.explanation: First reserve money for essentials and required minimum payments, then choose savings from available surplus before discretionary spending. A transfer is optional; no surplus means no transfer, without blame.

en.question: With PLN 4,000 take-home income, what is the illustrative 20% bucket?

answers.text: PLN 800

en.explanation: 4,000 × 20% = PLN 800. In this example, required minimum debt payments are included once in needs; the 20% bucket is savings and extra debt repayment. This is our illustration convention, not a compulsory split.

en.question: Which checklist is most complete when comparing savings accounts in Poland?

answers.text: Only the advertised interest rate
Rates and conditions, fees, access, and deposit protection
Whether the account guarantees an inflation-beating return
Whether your deposit is automatically invested in stocks

en.explanation: Check the rate and its duration, qualifying conditions, fees, withdrawal access, and the applicable deposit guarantee scheme. A deposit account is not a stock investment; inflation can still reduce purchasing power.

en.question: You invest PLN 100 twice, at PLN 10 then PLN 20 per unit. What do you buy?

answers.text: 10 units both times
5 units then 10 units
10 units then 5 units
A guaranteed profit

en.explanation: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 units; 100 ÷ 20 = 5 units. DCA uses equal amounts at regular intervals, not equal unit counts. At PLN 8 per unit, all 15 units are worth PLN 120 against PLN 200 invested: a PLN 80 loss, ignoring fees and taxes.

en.question: For one year, assumed nominal return is 2% and inflation 5%, with no fees, tax or cash flows. What is real return?

answers.text: Approximately −2.86%

en.explanation: PLN 1,000 becomes PLN 1,020 nominally, but 1,020 ÷ 1.05 ≈ PLN 971.43 in starting prices. Real return is approximately −2.86%; 2% − 5% = −3% is only a subtraction estimate, with fees/tax and cash flows excluded.

en.question: Assume a fixed 6% nominal rate, annual compounding and no fees, tax or cash flows. What does Rule of 72 estimate?

answers.text: 432 years, a guaranteed result
About 12 years to double, without a guarantee
0.08 years, a guaranteed result
Exactly 12 years even if rates change

en.explanation: Rule of 72 estimates nominal doubling: 72 ÷ a positive annual percentage rate. At an assumed fixed 6% with annual compounding/reinvestment and no cash flows, fees or tax, this is about 12 years. It is not an exact result, forecast or guarantee; inflation is excluded here.

en.question: Someone says an investment will always beat inflation. Which response is justified?

answers.text: Treat good past returns as a guarantee
Invest essential bill money to avoid inflation
Check loss risk, costs and access; gains are not guaranteed
A long holding period removes all loss risk

en.explanation: No investment automatically guarantees beating inflation. Check possible loss, costs and access to money. Past results and a long holding period are not guarantees. Protect essentials and required minimum repayments; postponing investment is an option when income varies.

en.question: After essentials and required minimums, PLN 100 remains. A PLN 1,000 debt charges 20% and a PLN 500 debt 10% annually; fixed rates, no fees, penalties or arrears. Where does avalanche direct the extra?

answers.text: Split equally, ignoring rates
To the smallest debt regardless of rate
To the debt charging 20%
Instead of another debt's minimum

en.explanation: After essentials and all required minimums, avalanche directs the available extra PLN 100 to the higher 20% rate. This model assumes fixed rates and no fees, penalties or arrears; actual prepayment terms depend on the contract. No extra payment is required without a surplus.

en.question: Which statement distinguishes BIK repayment history from repayment capacity in Poland?

answers.text: A high score guarantees a new loan
Timeliness matters; a lender also assesses income and expenses
Coachfi points replace a lender's assessment
Income does not matter for repayment capacity

en.explanation: Timely repayment matters for risk assessment. A lender also assesses income, expenses and debts, then makes its own decision. A BIK score does not guarantee a loan; Coachfi points are not a BIK score. No new debt or paid report is needed for the exercise.

en.question: You sell a fixed-cash-flow bond before maturity. Its required market yield rises, other factors unchanged. What happens to its price?

answers.text: It rises
It falls
The coupon automatically rises
Principal at maturity automatically falls

en.explanation: For the same fixed cash flows, a higher required yield means a lower secondary-market price. This does not automatically change the coupon or contractual principal at maturity. Sale price, redemption terms and default risk are distinct; this is not a rule for every bond.

en.question: Which decision conflicts with a readily accessible reserve with low volatility?

answers.text: Check access timing
Check fees and protection scope
Put the entire reserve in volatile shares
Distinguish reserves from planned spending

en.explanation: An entire reserve in volatile shares may lose value when needed. Check access, fees and terms; lower risk does not mean no losses or costs. Deposit protection depends on the institution and product, and does not cover every investment. This is not a provider choice.

en.question: Example: PLN 1,000 income, PLN 900 essentials, PLN 80 required minimums, no other costs or fees. Which small start fits these conditions?

answers.text: Transfer PLN 100 from a PLN 20 surplus
Optionally save PLN 10, leaving PLN 10
Borrow to save
Treat one month of costs as a required first threshold

en.explanation: 1,000 − 900 − 80 = PLN 20. An optional PLN 10 fits the surplus and leaves PLN 10; no transfer is required. At PLN 980 income, surplus is PLN 0. One month of expenses is not a required first goal; without funds, pause the transfer and do not borrow to save.

en.question: What is compound interest when credited interest stays in the balance?

answers.text: Interest only on the initial amount
An early withdrawal fee
Interest on principal and retained earlier interest
A certain profit from every investment

en.explanation: In a hypothetical model, PLN 1,000 at a constant 5% a year with annual compounding becomes PLN 1,050, then PLN 1,102.50. Interest stays; there are no contributions, withdrawals, fees or tax, and inflation is ignored. The extra PLN 2.50 is interest on the first PLN 50 of interest. This is a nominal model, not an offer or guaranteed investment profit.

en.question: What is the purpose of diversification, without guaranteeing no losses?

answers.text: Putting everything into one company
Spreading investments to reduce concentration risk
Ensuring a profit regardless of the market
Changing the portfolio weekly to ensure a profit

en.explanation: Different investments can reduce dependence on one issuer or sector. Multiple holdings may still share risks and fall together. Diversification does not guarantee profit or remove the risk of market losses.

en.question: What defines an index fund?

answers.text: Always having zero costs
An objective of tracking a specified index
Every ETF being an index fund
A guaranteed return above the market

en.explanation: An index fund seeks to track a specified index. Costs and tracking error can create differences in returns. Not every index fund is cheaper; check actual costs and risks. An ETF may track an index or be actively managed. The name does not promise market outperformance.

en.question: What does ETF mean?

answers.text: An account with guaranteed interest
A bank transfer fee
A fund whose shares trade on an exchange
A fund that always tracks a broad index

en.explanation: An ETF is an exchange-traded fund. It may follow an index or an active strategy and hold a narrow set of investments. An ETF alone does not ensure broad diversification or protect capital. Check holdings, risks, fees and buying and selling costs; losses are possible.

en.question: What belongs in an investment plan instead of assuming time alone guarantees profit?

answers.text: The date of a certain market bottom
Goals, horizon, reserves, acceptable losses and costs
Always selling after a 10% drop
Always holding every investment

en.explanation: A long horizon alone does not guarantee profit. A plan depends on goals, when money is needed, reserves, risk and costs; it can be reassessed when circumstances change. This is not an always-hold or sell-after-a-set-drop rule. Essentials and required minimums come first, and without surplus it is acceptable not to invest.

en.question: What is the purpose of planning finances for retirement?

answers.text: Certainty of maintaining every current income
Preparing resources for future needs after work changes or ends
Replacing emergency reserves with a risky investment
Doubling money simply by opening an account

en.explanation: A plan compares future needs and possible sources of funds; it does not guarantee maintaining current income. Emergency reserves have a separate role. Outcomes depend on contributions, conditions, costs and risk, among other factors. Essentials, required minimum repayments and reserves come first; without surplus, start with a free planning exercise, without buying anything or opening an account.

en.question: Model: PLN 1,000 once, a constant 5% a year, annual compounding, interest retained. No later contributions, withdrawals, fees or tax; inflation ignored. What is the nominal balance after 2 years?
en.explanation: In this hypothetical model, 1,000 × 1.05 × 1.05 = PLN 1,102.50. After year one the balance is PLN 1,050; the second interest payment is PLN 52.50. The positive result comes from the assumed constant rate, not time alone. More periods allow more compounding here, but actual outcomes can differ and losses are possible. This is not a pension forecast or a recommendation to contribute.

en.question: What can a survey percentage of correct answers about compound interest in Poland tell us?

answers.text: Everyone answering incorrectly will fall into debt
Knowledge alone guarantees a high pension
It is a result of specific questions, sample, year and scoring
That percentage describes all financial behaviour

en.explanation: Check the year, surveyed population, questions and scoring method. A knowledge result is not the same as behaviour or financial circumstances. A statistical association alone does not prove that lacking this knowledge directly causes debt or low retirement savings.

en.question: Does a survey percentage of stated trust establish that a particular institution is safe?

answers.text: Yes, if it has many customers
Yes, every higher percentage means no risk
Yes, if the result is older
No; a survey does not replace checking the institution

en.explanation: Check the date, sample and exact wording, including whether the question concerns institutions or their employees. Stated trust does not certify a particular institution or product as safe. A percentage alone also does not prove a cause of savings or wealth.

en.question: How should a gap to the maximum financial-literacy survey score be interpreted?

answers.text: As a certain amount of lost savings
As a point gap dependent on questions and scoring
As a future investment return
As proof that the respondent is to blame

en.explanation: Check the year, sample, instrument version and scoring key. A historical result does not automatically describe the current population. A point gap does not measure lost wealth and alone proves neither behaviour nor causes of financial difficulties.

en.question: What should be established before comparing PPK and PPE participation percentages?

answers.text: Only the highest percentage
That both names mean the same programme
The separate programme, date and group used for each percentage
That non-participation proves a lack of knowledge

en.explanation: PPK and PPE are separate arrangements. Identify the programme, date, surveyed group and denominator; do not combine percentages without a stated method. Participation statistics alone explain neither why people decide nor whether a lack of compound-interest knowledge caused that decision.

en.question: Which set most fully describes financial well-being in the CFPB framework?

answers.text: Only income level
Day-to-day finances, shock absorption, goals and freedom of choice
Only a financial quiz score
The number of financial products owned

en.explanation: The CFPB framework covers a sense of control over current finances, capacity to handle shocks, progress towards goals and freedom of choice. It is a descriptive framework, not a guarantee after mastering three tasks. Resources, circumstances and personal perceptions also matter; not everything depends on individual choices.

en.question: What best describes financial resilience?

answers.text: A guaranteed million in savings
An absolute absence of any debt
The capacity to handle a financial shock and rebuild one’s situation
Merely having an insurance policy

en.explanation: Income, resources, obligations, available support and the size of a shock matter, not just knowledge or mindset. A reserve may help but guarantees no coverage of every expense. Choose contributions voluntarily after essential needs and required minimum repayments; without a surplus, pause contributions.

en.question: Exercise: PLN 1000 debt, a hypothetical fixed 10% per period added to the debt. For 2 periods there are no repayments, fees or new borrowing. What is the balance?

answers.text: PLN 1000
PLN 1210
PLN 1200
PLN 2000

en.explanation: 1000 × 1.10 × 1.10 = PLN 1210. This is an assumed model, not an offer or a rule for every contract. Actual cost depends on terms and repayments. Debt difficulties can also involve lost income, unexpected costs and fees. A quiz establishes neither the cause of difficulties nor a person’s blame.

en.question: What is the main purpose of life insurance?

answers.text: To get rich when someone dies
To replace income for dependents if the primary earner dies
To save on taxes
To invest in the stock market safely

en.explanation: Life insurance protects dependents by replacing the primary earner's income if they die prematurely.

en.question: What is the recommended approach to finances for couples?

answers.text: One partner handles all finances, the other doesn't need to know
Both partners should understand the full financial picture and plan together
Keep all finances 100% separate — never share anything
Whoever earns more controls all decisions

en.explanation: Financial transparency and joint planning between partners leads to better decisions and fewer conflicts.

en.question: What is the most effective way to teach kids about money?

answers.text: Give them pocket money with no conditions
Let them observe — never discuss money with children
Give pocket money with saving rules (e.g. save 20%, spend 60%, give 20%)
Wait until they're 18 to discuss finances

en.explanation: Pocket money with saving/spending rules gives kids real financial decisions at low cost.

en.question: What inflation rate has the National Bank of Poland (NBP) targeted since 2004?

answers.text: 0% — prices should never rise
2.5% with a ±1 percentage point band
5% to encourage spending
Whatever the government sets each year

en.explanation: Since 2004 the NBP's target is 2.5% (±1 percentage point), measured by the annual change in the CPI.

en.question: Why do central banks aim for low, positive inflation (~2–2.5%) instead of 0%?

answers.text: To make the currency worthless faster
A small, stable buffer supports growth and avoids dangerous deflation
Because higher prices are always good
To increase government tax revenue only

en.explanation: A low, stable target avoids deflation (which can stall an economy) and keeps inflation predictable.

en.question: What is a central bank's main tool for steering inflation?

answers.text: Printing more banknotes for citizens
Setting benchmark interest rates
Fixing the price of bread
Banning imports

en.explanation: Central banks mainly use benchmark interest rates to influence borrowing, demand and ultimately inflation.

en.question: When a central bank raises interest rates, what typically happens?

answers.text: Borrowing gets cheaper and spending jumps
Borrowing gets more expensive, cooling demand and inflation
Nothing changes for households
Savings accounts always pay 0%

en.explanation: Rate hikes raise the cost of borrowing, which cools spending and helps bring inflation down.

en.question: What does GDP (Gross Domestic Product) measure?

answers.text: The total savings of all citizens
The value of all goods and services produced in an economy
The amount of cash in circulation
The national debt

en.explanation: GDP = the total market value of goods and services produced in a country over a period.

en.question: Why is persistent deflation (falling prices) considered dangerous?

answers.text: It makes everyone richer with no downside
People delay purchases, demand drops, and debts get harder to repay
It always boosts wages
It has no effect on the economy

en.explanation: Deflation pushes people to delay spending and makes existing debt heavier in real terms — a dangerous loop.

en.question: What does “zero” mean in zero-based budgeting?

answers.text: You must spend everything and empty the account
Every available unit has a purpose in the plan, including reserves
Savings must equal zero
Only cash may be used

en.explanation: This is a planning method, not a requirement to spend everything or empty an account. Hypothetically: PLN 1000 = 800 for essential needs + 100 for required minimum repayments + 100 for a voluntary reserve; unallocated: PLN 0. Repayments are counted once. Update the plan when income varies; no surplus means no duty to save. The plan does not guarantee freedom from unexpected expenses.

en.question: What can help you understand spending before making or revising a budget?

answers.text: First postpone urgent essential purchases for 30 days
Optionally review your own spending over a suitable period using a method you choose
Everyone must first collect exactly 30 days of data
Borrow money instead of checking spending

en.explanation: You can start with a day or week of your own notes and extend the period; 30 days is not a mandatory prerequisite. Include less frequent bills and variable income too. Do not postpone urgent essential needs or required minimum repayments while observing. Choose a manageable method and return when you can; you do not need to share data with the app.

en.question: You have PLN 0 saved for an optional PLN 600 purchase in 6 months. What are 6 equal monthly contributions before purchase, ignoring interest and fees?

answers.text: PLN 600 each month
PLN 100 each month for this planned goal
PLN 0, because reserves guarantee every cost is covered
Borrowing always replaces such a plan

en.explanation: 600 ÷ 6 = PLN 100 monthly in this hypothetical plan. A sinking fund is for a known future cost; emergency reserves cover unexpected events. Contributions are voluntary, after essential needs and required minimum repayments. With no surplus, change the goal or postpone this optional purchase; update the plan when income varies. There is no guarantee of avoiding debt.

en.question: What could you optionally do before a non-urgent, non-essential purchase?

answers.text: Always buy immediately and check the cost later
Take a pause you choose and check the need, price and plan
Postpone urgent essential purchases too
Assume every pause guarantees savings

en.explanation: You can pause and return to the decision at a suitable time. This is an option, not a mandatory 24 hours or a guarantee of savings or a change in desire to buy. Do not postpone urgent essential needs or required minimum repayments. After a break, calmly check the price, available money and priorities; you can revise the decision without pressure.

en.question: After covering essentials and all required minimum repayments, PLN 20 remains. Which small first step is an optional choice in this example?

answers.text: Save a full month of costs at once as a requirement
Choose e.g. PLN 5; pause if there is no surplus
Borrow PLN 100 to start a reserve
Transfer all income before paying bills

en.explanation: Example budget: PLN 1,200 income − PLN 1,080 essentials − PLN 100 required minimums = PLN 20 surplus, with no other costs or fees. An optional PLN 5 leaves PLN 15; no transfer is required. Adapt the goal to circumstances without requiring a full month at the start. Without surplus, pause; do not borrow to save.

en.question: In Poland, up to what amount are bank deposits guaranteed by the BFG?

answers.text: There is no deposit guarantee
The PLN equivalent of €100,000 per depositor, per bank
Exactly 10,000 PLN total
Unlimited, always 100%

en.explanation: Poland's BFG guarantees deposits up to the PLN equivalent of €100,000 per depositor in each bank.

en.question: What is the general relationship between risk and expected return?

answers.text: Higher expected returns generally come with higher risk
High returns are guaranteed with zero risk
Risk and return are unrelated
Lower risk always means higher return

en.explanation: Higher potential return generally requires taking on more risk. Be sceptical of 'high return, no risk' offers.

en.question: How should beginners treat highly speculative assets like crypto?

answers.text: Put all savings in for maximum gains
Limit to a small share you could afford to lose entirely
Borrow money to buy more
Treat it as a safe emergency fund

en.explanation: Keep speculative assets to a small portion of your portfolio, and only money you can afford to lose completely.

en.question: What's the key tax difference between Poland's IKE and IKZE accounts?

answers.text: They are identical in every way
IKE: tax-free gains on a qualifying withdrawal; IKZE: deduct contributions now, pay a 10% flat tax on withdrawal
Both are taxed at 19% every year
Neither offers any tax benefit

en.explanation: IKE = tax-free growth on qualifying withdrawal. IKZE = deduct contributions today, 10% flat tax when you withdraw.

en.question: In Poland's PPK, what does the employer add on top of the employee's 2% basic contribution?

answers.text: Nothing — only the employee pays
A basic 1.5% of salary (plus an optional extra up to 2.5%)
A flat 100 PLN regardless of salary
10% of salary

en.explanation: PPK: employee 2% basic, employer adds 1.5% basic (up to +2.5% extra). The employer match is free retirement money.

en.question: What state incentives does Poland's PPK give participants?

answers.text: No state support at all
A 250 PLN welcome payment and a 240 PLN annual bonus
A 50,000 PLN lump sum
Free shares in the employer

en.explanation: PPK state support: a one-off 250 PLN welcome payment and a 240 PLN annual bonus for participants.

en.question: What do deposit guarantee schemes (BFG, FDIC, EU DGS, FGC) actually protect?

answers.text: All investments including stocks and crypto
Bank deposits — not stocks, funds, pensions or crypto
Only cash kept at home
Your salary if you lose your job

en.explanation: These schemes protect bank deposits only. Stocks, funds, pensions and crypto fall outside them.

en.question: In the United States, how much does the FDIC insure per depositor, per bank?

answers.text: $250,000 (per ownership category)
Unlimited
There is no deposit insurance in the US

en.explanation: US FDIC coverage is $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each ownership category.

en.question: Across the EU (incl. Poland, Spain, France), bank deposits are guaranteed up to…

answers.text: €1,000 per country
€100,000 per depositor, per bank (or local-currency equivalent)
Nothing is guaranteed in the EU

en.explanation: EU rules harmonise deposit protection at €100,000 per depositor, per bank.

en.question: With a US 401(k) that offers an employer match, what's the smartest first move?

answers.text: Skip it — matches are a trick
Contribute at least enough to get the full employer match (free money)
Only contribute after age 60
Put it all into a single company stock

en.explanation: Always contribute enough to capture the full employer match — it's free money you can't get any other way.

en.question: What do a UK ISA, a Japanese NISA and a Polish IKE have in common?

answers.text: They guarantee a fixed 10% return
They are tax-advantaged accounts that shelter investment growth
They are types of credit card
They are only for millionaires

en.explanation: ISA (UK), NISA (Japan) and IKE (Poland) are tax-advantaged accounts that shelter investment gains.

en.question: What inflation target does India's central bank (RBI) aim for?

answers.text: 4% with a ±2 percentage point tolerance band
It has no target

en.explanation: India's RBI targets 4% inflation with a tolerance band of ±2 percentage points (2–6%).

en.question: How should 50/30/20 be understood as a flexible guide for take-home income?

answers.text: 50% savings, 30% needs, 20% wants
50% needs, 30% wants, 20% savings and debt payments
Always save 20%, even at the expense of essential bills
Borrow in order to save exactly 20%

en.explanation: 50/30/20 is an illustrative split of take-home income that can be adapted. First protect essential needs and required minimum repayments; do not count the same payment twice. Adjust amounts when income varies. Without a surplus, do not force 20% saving.

en.question: Model: PLN 1,000, a constant hypothetical 5% a year, annual compounding, interest retained. No contributions, withdrawals, fees or tax; inflation ignored. Nominal balance after 2 years?
en.explanation: Compounding adds interest on retained earlier interest. In the model, 1,000 × 1.05 × 1.05 = PLN 1,102.50. The positive result depends on the assumed 5%, not time alone. This is a hypothetical calculation, with no guarantee of actual gains; investments can lose value.

en.question: Which statement describes diversification and its limit?

answers.text: Everything in one strong company
Different assets can reduce concentration; losses remain possible
One bond removes every risk
Frequent trades guarantee protection from a decline

en.explanation: Diversification spreads exposure across different assets and can reduce concentration risk. It does not remove market risk or guarantee avoiding losses. Different fund names may hide similar holdings; check holdings, risk and costs. No purchase is required.

en.question: How does a debt avalanche work once essentials and all required minimum repayments are covered?

answers.text: Finances every extra payment with a new loan
Always starts with the smallest balance
Puts an available extra payment toward the highest-rate debt
Skips required payments on other debts

en.explanation: An avalanche puts available extra money toward the highest rate after essentials and every debt minimum. With fixed rates and no extra fees, it can reduce interest. Check fees and consequences of arrears; without a surplus, do not force an extra payment. It does not guarantee the lowest total cost under all conditions.

en.question: Hypothetical: nominal return +2% and inflation 5% over the same year, no fees or tax. What is the rounded real return?

answers.text: About −2.86%

en.explanation: The exact relation is (1.02 ÷1.05 −1) × 100% ≈ −2.86%. Subtracting 2% −5% =−3% is an approximation. Initial PLN 1,000 becomes nominal PLN 1,020, or about PLN 971.43 in initial prices. The model uses the same year and no fees or tax; it is not a current offer.

en.question: Which statement about funds is correct?

answers.text: Every ETF always tracks an index
An index fund tracks an index; an ETF can be indexed or active
Every index fund is the cheapest
Every ETF guarantees beating the market

en.explanation: An index fund aims to track an index. An ETF is an exchange-traded fund structure; it can be indexed or active. Neither label guarantees low costs, beating the market or avoiding losses. Check the objective, holdings, risk and all costs. You do not have to invest.

en.question: Which statement describes DCA?

answers.text: Investing the whole amount only at the lowest price
Selling everything after every decline
An equal amount at regular intervals, regardless of price
Converting savings into dollars

en.explanation: DCA uses an equal amount at regular intervals; a lower price buys more units. It guarantees neither profit nor protection from loss and does not automatically remove emotions. With no fees or tax: PLN 100 at 10 and PLN 100 at 20 buys 15 units. At 8 they are worth PLN 120 versus PLN 200 contributed. Contributions are optional, after essentials and required minimum repayments.

en.question: Rule 72: a hypothetical constant positive 8% nominal annual rate, annual compounding, no contributions, withdrawals, fees or tax; inflation ignored. What doubling-time estimate does the rule give?

answers.text: About 6 years
About 9 years
About 72 years
Exactly 9 years for every investment

en.explanation: 72 ÷8 ≈ 9 years is an approximation, not an exact date. In the model, 1,000 × 1.08⁹ ≈ PLN 1,999.00; after 10 annual credits it exceeds PLN 2,000. A constant positive 8% is an assumption, not a forecast. Actual rates may change and investments can lose value. This nominal model excludes cash flows, fees, tax and inflation.

en.question: What is an ETF?

answers.text: A deposit guaranteeing a stated interest payment
An electronic transfer fee
An exchange-traded fund, indexed or actively managed
A government emergency reserve

en.explanation: An ETF is an exchange-traded fund. It may track an index or be actively managed. Diversification depends on actual holdings; a narrow-sector fund can be concentrated. The label guarantees neither low costs nor freedom from loss. Check objectives, holdings, risks and costs; no purchase is required.

en.question: Which choice does NOT fit the purpose of an emergency reserve?

answers.text: Ready access for an unexpected expense
A situation-based goal and small achievable start
High-risk stocks solely for maximum growth
Keeping the reserve separate from everyday spending

en.explanation: A reserve aims to make funds accessible for unexpected needs with limited risk, rather than maximize returns. Keep it separate from everyday spending. Size depends on circumstances;3–6 months is an optional guide, not a duty or guarantee. Start voluntarily after essentials and required minimum repayments; without a surplus, pause contributions.

en.question: What generally happens to an existing fixed-coupon bond’s secondary-market price when comparable market yields rise and all other conditions stay equal?

answers.text: The price rises
The price falls
The price always equals face value
The price must double

en.explanation: With fixed cash flows and all else equal, a higher market yield means a lower secondary-market price. The agreed coupon does not rise automatically. A sale price before maturity differs from contractual payments. Repayment also depends on the issuer’s ability to pay; default and liquidity risk remain.

en.question: Hypothetically, monthly income rises by PLN 200 and discretionary spending by PLN 180; essentials and required minimum repayments are unchanged. How much does the surplus rise?

answers.text: PLN 200
PLN 180
PLN 20
It can never change

en.explanation: 200 − 180 = PLN 20 of extra monthly surplus. Discretionary spending rising with income illustrates lifestyle inflation, distinct from rising prices and necessary costs. Not every pay rise must be saved. Adapt the plan to essentials, required minimum repayments, goals and variable income; this is not a judgment of the person.

en.question: What is the main purpose of long-term retirement planning?

answers.text: Guaranteed doubling of every balance
Preparing resources for future needs when work changes or ends
Replacing an emergency reserve with a risky investment
A certain tax benefit for every payment and every account

en.explanation: Planning helps prepare resources for future needs but guarantees neither full income replacement nor profit. A retirement goal alone does not give every account a tax benefit. Essentials, required minimum repayments and reserves come before optional investment. Adjust or pause contributions when income varies.

en.question: Hypothetically on a given date: assets PLN 50,000 and liabilities PLN 20,000. What is net worth?

answers.text: Monthly salary

en.explanation: Net worth =assets −liabilities:50,000 − 20,000 = PLN 30,000 on that date. It is a wealth snapshot, not monthly income and expense flows or available cash. It does not define overall financial well-being or a person’s worth. Valuations and liabilities may change.

en.question: Hypothetical month: PLN 100 remains after essentials and required repayments; no other funds are available. A new payment is PLN 150. What does the budget show?

answers.text: Knowing compound interest covers the missing PLN 50
An unconfirmed pay rise guarantees repayment
PLN 50 is missing; check costs and affordability before deciding
Borrow PLN 50 and assume the budget is unchanged

en.explanation: 100 − 150 = −PLN 50. Essentials and existing required repayments have already been deducted once in this example. Knowing compound interest alone does not provide income or ensure repayment. Before a new commitment, check full costs, dates and a realistic budget; allow for fluctuations with variable income. Another loan does not prove that this payment is covered by the stated budget.

en.question: Which checklist is most complete when comparing surveys of trust in financial institutions?

answers.text: Only the publication headline
Only the year, without sample information
The number of likes on the publication
Year, sample, question wording and measurement method

en.explanation: Check who was surveyed, when, what was asked and how the result was calculated. Different questions or samples limit comparability. Declared trust is not a certificate that a particular institution is safe or proof of an effect on wealth.

en.question: Exercise: a made-up 0–21-point scale gives a score of 13. What does the gap to the maximum mean?

answers.text: 8 lost opportunities for profit
8 points under the chosen scoring key, not a wealth diagnosis
8 months without money
8 people without an account

en.explanation: 21 − 13 = 8 points in this exercise. This made-up scale is not the current OECD scale; points are not a count of questions. Points alone prove neither behaviour, debt, resilience nor the causes of difficulties. Survey results need a year, sample, questions and scoring key; measurement versions can differ.

en.question: Exercise: this month, PLN 50 remains after essential needs and required minimum repayments. Which step is voluntary and fits within that amount?

answers.text: Borrow PLN 100 to make a compulsory saving of 100
Skip a required repayment
Choose PLN 10 for a reserve and leave PLN 40
Assume a small transfer will remove all stress

en.explanation: 50 − 10 = PLN 40 in the same month; essentials and required repayments were already counted once. A small step is an option, not a duty or a guarantee of no stress. Without a surplus, pause contributions; do not borrow to save. When income varies, return to the plan and adjust the amount.

en.question: Which Polish term means money set aside for unexpected, unplanned expenses?

answers.text: Pay for current work
Poduszka finansowa (emergency reserve)
A required loan to fund savings
A certain investment profit

en.explanation: An emergency reserve is kept separately for unexpected expenses. Adapt the goal to your circumstances; a small start is voluntary, with no single mandatory threshold. First protect essential needs and required minimum repayments; without a surplus, pause contributions. Check access and risk; a reserve cannot automatically cover every event.

en.question: What do attitudes towards money describe in a survey?

answers.text: The number of products owned
Income level and wealth
Stated views on spending, saving and the future
Guaranteed repayment capacity

en.explanation: These are stated views, such as spending today versus saving for the future. They are not a knowledge test or a full measure of behaviour or financial circumstances. Stated views alone prove neither the cause of difficulties nor a future outcome. Income and essential costs also shape possibilities; avoid judging the person.

pl.question: Ten sam ważony koszyk kosztuje 1 000 zł, potem 1 050 zł. Co pokazuje ten przykład?

answers.text: Każda cena musi wzrosnąć o 5%
Koszyk drożeje o 5%; ta sama gotówka kupuje mniej
Koszty każdego gospodarstwa rosną dokładnie o 5%
Jedna wyższa cena dowodzi ogólnej inflacji

pl.explanation: Inflacja dotyczy ogólnego wzrostu cen ważonego koszyka, nie jednej ceny. Tutaj (1 050 ÷ 1 000 − 1) × 100% = 5%; ta sama gotówka kupuje mniej tego koszyka. Gospodarstwa mają różne koszyki wydatków.

pl.question: W przykładzie wybierasz 3 miesiące po 2 000 zł niezbędnych kosztów (w tym wymagane minimum długu, liczone raz). Ile wynosi cel przy stałych kosztach?
pl.explanation: 3 × 2 000 zł = 6 000 zł przy podanych stałych kosztach, z minimum długu już uwzględnionym raz. Wielkość rezerwy zależy od sytuacji; 3–6 miesięcy można wybrać orientacyjnie, bez gwarancji ochrony. To nie termin zebrania kwoty ani obowiązek przelewu.

pl.question: Który przelew jest bezpieczny przy zmiennym dochodzie?

answers.text: Odkładać stałą kwotę mimo nieopłaconych rachunków
Pożyczać pieniądze, aby oszczędzać co miesiąc
Wybrać dostępną kwotę po potrzebach i minimalnych spłatach
Przelać cały dochód przed sprawdzeniem przyszłych rachunków

pl.explanation: Najpierw zabezpiecz potrzeby i wymagane minimalne spłaty. Następnie wybierz opcjonalny przelew z dostępnej nadwyżki. Przy zmiennym dochodzie sprawdzaj kwotę i termin; bez nadwyżki wstrzymaj przelew.

pl.question: Hipotetyczny kredyt: wskaźnik 3% + marża 2 pkt proc. Przy umownej aktualizacji wskaźnik rośnie do 4%, marża bez zmian. Jakie jest nowe oprocentowanie?
pl.explanation: Nowy wskaźnik zastępuje stary: 4% + niezmieniona marża 2 pkt proc. = 6%. Termin określa umowa; sama decyzja banku centralnego nie oznacza natychmiastowej zmiany każdej raty. Oprocentowanie może być stałe lub okresowo stałe. Sprawdź uzgodniony okres i dalsze warunki umowy po jego końcu; nie oznacza to zamrożenia wszystkich opłat.

pl.question: Co oznacza wartość netto?

answers.text: Miesięczna pensja po podatku
Aktywa minus zobowiązania
Gotówka w portfelu
Ocena kredytowa

pl.explanation: Wartość netto to aktywa minus zobowiązania na ten sam dzień. Dochód jest przepływem, a gotówka i ocena kredytowa to inne miary. Sama wartość netto nie opisuje płynności ani wartości człowieka.

pl.question: Co oznacza inflacja stylu życia?

answers.text: Podnoszenie płacy minimalnej przez państwo
Ceny rosną szybciej niż pensje
Dobrowolne zwiększanie wydatków na standard życia wraz ze wzrostem dochodu
Ubarwianie swojego CV

pl.explanation: Inflacja stylu życia to dobrowolny wzrost wydatków uznaniowych wraz z dochodem. To co innego niż wzrost cen lub konieczne wydatki i nie oznacza, że każda podwyżka jest wydawana w całości.

pl.question: Co oznacza zasada zapłać najpierw sobie?

answers.text: Najpierw wydawać na przyjemności
Planować oszczędności z nadwyżki po zabezpieczeniu potrzeb i wymaganych minimalnych spłat
Najpierw podnieść sobie pensję
Kupić luksusowe rzeczy przed zakupami spożywczymi

pl.explanation: Najpierw zabezpiecz potrzeby i wymagane minimalne spłaty, potem wybierz oszczędności z dostępnej nadwyżki przed wydatkami uznaniowymi. Przelew jest opcjonalny; brak nadwyżki oznacza brak przelewu, bez poczucia winy.

pl.question: Przy dochodzie 4 000 zł na rękę ile wynosi przykładowa część 20%?

answers.text: 800 zł

pl.explanation: 4 000 × 20% = 800 zł. W tym przykładzie wymagane minimalne spłaty długu liczymy raz w potrzebach; część 20% obejmuje oszczędności i dodatkowe spłaty. To konwencja naszego przykładu, nie obowiązkowy podział.

pl.question: Która lista jest najpełniejsza przy porównywaniu kont oszczędnościowych w Polsce?

answers.text: Tylko reklamowane oprocentowanie
Oprocentowanie i warunki, opłaty, dostęp i ochronę depozytów
Czy konto gwarantuje wynik powyżej inflacji
Czy wpłata jest automatycznie inwestowana w akcje

pl.explanation: Sprawdź oprocentowanie i czas jego obowiązywania, warunki, opłaty, dostęp do wypłat oraz właściwy system gwarantowania depozytów. Konto depozytowe to nie inwestycja w akcje; inflacja nadal może obniżać siłę nabywczą.

pl.question: Wpłacasz dwa razy po 100 zł, przy cenach 10 zł i 20 zł za jednostkę. Ile kupujesz?

answers.text: Za każdym razem 10 jednostek
Najpierw 5, potem 10 jednostek
Najpierw 10, potem 5 jednostek
Gwarantowany zysk

pl.explanation: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 jednostek; 100 ÷ 20 = 5 jednostek. DCA oznacza równe kwoty w regularnych odstępach, nie równą liczbę jednostek. Przy cenie 8 zł wszystkie 15 jednostek są warte 120 zł wobec wpłat 200 zł: strata 80 zł, bez opłat i podatków.

pl.question: Przez rok założony nominalny zwrot to 2%, a inflacja 5%, bez opłat, podatku i przepływów. Jaki jest realny zwrot?

answers.text: Około −2,86%

pl.explanation: 1 000 zł zmienia się nominalnie w 1 020 zł, lecz 1 020 ÷ 1,05 ≈ 971,43 zł w cenach początku przykładu. Realny zwrot to około −2,86%; 2% − 5% = −3% jest tylko przybliżeniem przez odejmowanie, bez opłat, podatku i przepływów.

pl.question: Załóż stałe nominalne 6%, roczną kapitalizację, brak opłat, podatku i przepływów. Co szacuje reguła 72?

answers.text: 432 lata, gwarantowany wynik
Około 12 lat do podwojenia, bez gwarancji
0,08 roku, gwarantowany wynik
Dokładnie 12 lat nawet przy zmianach stopy

pl.explanation: Reguła 72 szacuje nominalne podwojenie: 72 ÷ dodatnia roczna stopa w procentach. Przy założonych stałych 6%, rocznej kapitalizacji/reinwestowaniu i bez przepływów, opłat lub podatku wychodzi około 12 lat. To nie wynik dokładny, prognoza ani gwarancja; tutaj pomijamy inflację.

pl.question: Ktoś zapewnia, że inwestycja zawsze pokona inflację. Która odpowiedź jest uzasadniona?

answers.text: Uznaj dobre dawne wyniki za gwarancję
Zainwestuj środki na niezbędne rachunki
Sprawdź ryzyko straty, koszty i dostęp; zysk nie jest pewny
Długi okres usuwa całe ryzyko straty

pl.explanation: Żadna inwestycja automatycznie nie gwarantuje pokonania inflacji. Sprawdź możliwość straty, koszty i dostęp do pieniędzy. Dawne wyniki i długi czas nie są gwarancją. Chroń niezbędne wydatki i wymagane minimalne spłaty; przy zmiennych dochodach możesz odłożyć inwestowanie.

pl.question: Po potrzebach i wymaganych minimalnych spłatach zostaje 100 zł. Dług 1 000 zł ma 20%, a 500 zł 10% rocznie; stopy stałe, brak opłat, kar i zaległości. Gdzie kieruje nadwyżkę lawina?

answers.text: Po równo, ignorując stopy
Na najmniejszy dług bez względu na stopę
Na dług oprocentowany 20%
Zamiast minimum innego długu

pl.explanation: Po podstawowych potrzebach i wymaganych minimalnych spłatach lawina kieruje dostępne dodatkowe 100 zł na wyższą stopę 20%. Model zakłada stałe stopy, brak opłat, kar i zaległości; rzeczywiste warunki nadpłaty sprawdza się w umowie. Brak nadwyżki nie wymaga nadpłaty.

pl.question: Które stwierdzenie odróżnia historię w BIK od zdolności kredytowej w Polsce?

answers.text: Wysoki wynik gwarantuje nowy kredyt
Terminowość jest istotna; bank bada też dochody i wydatki
Punkty Coachfi zastępują ocenę banku
Dochody nie mają znaczenia dla zdolności

pl.explanation: Terminowość spłat jest istotna dla oceny ryzyka. Bank ocenia również dochody, wydatki i zobowiązania oraz podejmuje własną decyzję. Wynik BIK nie gwarantuje kredytu; punkty Coachfi nie są oceną BIK. Nie trzeba brać nowego długu ani kupować raportu, aby wykonać ćwiczenie.

pl.question: Przed wykupem sprzedajesz obligację o stałych przepływach. Wymagana rentowność rynkowa rośnie, inne czynniki bez zmian. Co dzieje się z ceną?

answers.text: Rośnie
Spada
Kupon automatycznie rośnie
Nominał przy wykupie automatycznie maleje

pl.explanation: Dla tych samych stałych przepływów wyższa wymagana rentowność oznacza niższą cenę na rynku wtórnym. Nie zmienia to automatycznie kuponu ani umownego nominału przy wykupie. Cena sprzedaży, warunki wykupu i ryzyko niewypłacalności to różne sprawy; to nie reguła dla każdej obligacji.

pl.question: Która decyzja przeczy celowi szybko dostępnej rezerwy o niskiej zmienności?

answers.text: Sprawdzenie czasu dostępu
Sprawdzenie opłat i zakresu ochrony
Cała rezerwa w zmiennych akcjach
Odróżnienie rezerwy od planowanych wydatków

pl.explanation: Cała rezerwa w zmiennych akcjach może stracić wartość, gdy jest potrzebna. Sprawdź dostęp, opłaty i warunki; niskie ryzyko nie oznacza braku strat lub kosztów. Ochrona depozytu zależy od podmiotu i produktu, a nie każda inwestycja jest objęta ochroną. To nie wybór dostawcy.

pl.question: Przykład: wpływ 1 000 zł, potrzeby 900 zł, wymagane minima 80 zł, brak innych kosztów i opłat. Który mały start mieści się w tych warunkach?

answers.text: Przelać 100 zł, choć nadwyżka to tylko 20 zł
Dobrowolnie odłożyć 10 zł, pozostawiając 10 zł
Pożyczyć na oszczędzanie
Uznać miesiąc kosztów za obowiązkowy próg startu

pl.explanation: 1 000 − 900 − 80 = 20 zł. Dobrowolne 10 zł mieści się w nadwyżce i zostawia 10 zł; nie ma obowiązku przelewu. Przy 980 zł wpływu nadwyżka to 0 zł. Miesiąc wydatków nie jest wymaganym pierwszym celem; przy braku środków wstrzymaj przelew, nie pożyczaj na oszczędzanie.

pl.question: Co oznacza procent składany, gdy dopisane odsetki zostają w saldzie?

answers.text: Odsetki wyłącznie od kwoty początkowej
Opłatę za wcześniejszą wypłatę
Odsetki od kapitału i pozostawionych wcześniejszych odsetek
Pewny zysk z każdej inwestycji

pl.explanation: W hipotetycznym modelu 1 000 zł przy stałych 5% rocznie i kapitalizacji rocznej daje 1 050 zł, potem 1 102,50 zł. Odsetki zostają; brak dopłat, wypłat, opłat i podatku, inflacja pominięta. Dodatkowe 2,50 zł pochodzi z odsetek od pierwszych 50 zł odsetek. To model nominalny, nie oferta lub gwarancja zysku z inwestycji.

pl.question: Co jest celem dywersyfikacji, bez gwarancji uniknięcia strat?

answers.text: Ulokowanie wszystkiego w jednej spółce
Rozłożenie inwestycji, by ograniczyć ryzyko koncentracji
Zapewnienie zysku niezależnie od rynku
Cotygodniowa zmiana portfela zapewniająca zysk

pl.explanation: Różne inwestycje mogą ograniczyć zależność od jednego emitenta lub sektora. Wiele pozycji może jednak mieć podobne ryzyko i spadać jednocześnie. Dywersyfikacja nie gwarantuje zysku i nie usuwa ryzyka strat rynkowych.

pl.question: Co określa fundusz indeksowy?

answers.text: Zawsze zerowe koszty
Cel odwzorowania wskazanego indeksu
To, że każdy ETF jest indeksowy
Gwarantowany wynik lepszy od rynku

pl.explanation: Fundusz indeksowy dąży do odwzorowania wskazanego indeksu. Koszty i błąd odwzorowania mogą powodować różnice wyniku. Nie każdy fundusz indeksowy jest tańszy; sprawdź rzeczywiste koszty i ryzyko. ETF może być indeksowy albo aktywnie zarządzany. Sama nazwa nie obiecuje przewagi nad rynkiem.

pl.question: Co oznacza ETF?

answers.text: Konto z gwarantowanymi odsetkami
Opłatę za przelew
Fundusz, którego tytuły są notowane na giełdzie
Fundusz zawsze śledzący szeroki indeks

pl.explanation: ETF to fundusz notowany na giełdzie. Może mieć strategię indeksową lub aktywną i wąski zakres inwestycji. Sam ETF nie zapewnia szerokiej dywersyfikacji ani ochrony kapitału. Sprawdź skład, ryzyko, opłaty oraz koszty zakupu i sprzedaży; można ponieść stratę.

pl.question: Co uwzględnić w planie inwestowania zamiast zakładać pewny zysk dzięki samemu czasowi?

answers.text: Datę pewnego dołka rynku
Cel, horyzont, rezerwę, akceptowane straty i koszty
Sprzedaż zawsze po spadku o 10%
Trzymanie każdej inwestycji zawsze

pl.explanation: Długi horyzont sam nie gwarantuje zysku. Plan zależy od celu, terminu potrzeby pieniędzy, rezerwy, ryzyka i kosztów; można go ponownie ocenić, gdy zmienią się okoliczności. Nie ma tu reguły zawsze trzymaj ani sprzedaj po określonym spadku. Potrzeby i wymagane minimum są pierwsze, a brak nadwyżki pozwala nie inwestować.

pl.question: Jaki jest cel planowania finansów na emeryturę?

answers.text: Pewność utrzymania każdego dzisiejszego dochodu
Przygotowanie środków na przyszłe potrzeby po zmianie lub zakończeniu pracy
Zastąpienie rezerwy awaryjnej ryzykowną inwestycją
Podwojenie środków przez samo otwarcie konta

pl.explanation: Plan porównuje przyszłe potrzeby i możliwe źródła środków; nie gwarantuje utrzymania dzisiejszego dochodu. Rezerwa awaryjna ma odrębną rolę. Wynik zależy m.in. od wpłat, warunków, kosztów i ryzyka. Potrzeby, wymagane minimalne spłaty i rezerwa są pierwsze; bez nadwyżki można zacząć od bezkosztowego planu, bez zakupu lub otwierania konta.

pl.question: Model: 1 000 zł jednorazowo, stałe 5% rocznie, kapitalizacja roczna, odsetki zostają. Bez dopłat, wypłat, opłat i podatku; inflacja pominięta. Ile nominalnie po 2 latach?
pl.explanation: W tym hipotetycznym modelu 1 000 × 1,05 × 1,05 = 1 102,50 zł. Po pierwszym roku jest 1 050 zł; drugie odsetki to 52,50 zł. Dodatni wynik wynika z założonej stałej stopy, nie z samego upływu czasu. Więcej okresów daje tu więcej kapitalizacji, ale rzeczywiste wyniki mogą być inne i straty są możliwe. To nie prognoza emerytury ani zalecenie wpłaty.

pl.question: Co można wywnioskować z odsetka poprawnych odpowiedzi w badaniu wiedzy o procencie składanym w Polsce?

answers.text: Każda osoba z błędną odpowiedzią wpadnie w długi
Sama wiedza gwarantuje wysoką emeryturę
To wynik określonych pytań, próby, roku i punktowania
Ten odsetek opisuje wszystkie zachowania finansowe

pl.explanation: Sprawdź rok, badaną populację, treść pytań i sposób punktowania. Wynik wiedzy nie jest tym samym co zachowanie ani sytuacja finansowa. Sama zależność statystyczna nie dowodzi, że brak tej wiedzy bezpośrednio powoduje długi lub niskie oszczędności emerytalne.

pl.question: Czy odsetek deklarowanego zaufania w ankiecie potwierdza bezpieczeństwo konkretnej instytucji?

answers.text: Tak, jeśli ma dużo klientów
Tak, każdy większy odsetek oznacza brak ryzyka
Tak, jeśli wynik jest starszy
Nie; ankieta nie zastępuje sprawdzenia konkretnej instytucji

pl.explanation: Sprawdź datę, próbę i dokładną treść pytania, np. czy dotyczy instytucji czy ich pracowników. Deklarowane zaufanie nie certyfikuje bezpieczeństwa konkretnej instytucji lub produktu. Sam odsetek nie dowodzi też przyczyny oszczędności ani majątku.

pl.question: Jak interpretować różnicę do maksimum wyniku w badaniu kompetencji finansowych?

answers.text: Jako pewną kwotę straconych oszczędności
Jako różnicę punktów zależną od pytań i klucza
Jako przyszłą stopę zwrotu
Jako dowód winy badanej osoby

pl.explanation: Sprawdź rok, próbę, wersję narzędzia i klucz punktowania. Historyczny wynik nie opisuje automatycznie obecnej populacji. Różnica punktów nie mierzy kwoty utraconego majątku i sama nie dowodzi zachowania ani przyczyn problemów finansowych.

pl.question: Co ustalić przed porównaniem odsetków uczestnictwa w PPK i PPE?

answers.text: Tylko najwyższy odsetek
Że obie nazwy oznaczają ten sam program

Że brak udziału dowodzi braku wiedzy

pl.explanation: PPK i PPE to odrębne rozwiązania. Ustal program, datę oraz badaną grupę i mianownik; nie łącz odsetków bez określonej metody. Sama statystyka uczestnictwa nie wyjaśnia powodów decyzji ani nie dowodzi, że jej przyczyną jest brak wiedzy o procencie składanym.

pl.question: Który zestaw najpełniej oddaje dobrostan finansowy w ujęciu CFPB?

answers.text: Tylko wysokość dochodu
Codzienne finanse, odporność na wstrząsy, cele i swoboda wyboru
Sam wynik quizu finansowego
Liczba posiadanych produktów

pl.explanation: Ujęcie CFPB obejmuje poczucie kontroli nad bieżącymi finansami, możliwość radzenia sobie ze wstrząsami, realizację celów i swobodę wyborów. To rama opisu, nie gwarancja po opanowaniu trzech zadań. Znaczenie mają też zasoby, otoczenie i własne odczucia; nie wszystko zależy od decyzji osoby.

pl.question: Co najlepiej opisuje odporność finansową?

answers.text: Gwarantowana milionowa kwota oszczędności
Bezwzględny brak każdego długu
Zdolność radzenia sobie ze szokiem finansowym i odbudowy sytuacji
Sama obecność polisy

pl.explanation: Znaczenie mają dochód, zasoby, zobowiązania, dostępna pomoc i skala szoku, nie tylko wiedza lub nastawienie. Rezerwa może pomóc, ale nie gwarantuje pokrycia każdego wydatku. Wpłaty wybieraj dobrowolnie po podstawowych potrzebach i wymaganych minimalnych spłatach; bez nadwyżki wstrzymaj wpłatę.

pl.question: Ćwiczenie: dług 1000 zł, stałe hipotetyczne 10% za okres dopisywane do długu. Przez 2 okresy brak spłat, opłat i nowego długu. Ile wynosi saldo?

Dług publiczny

Hipotetycznie: 1000 zł = 800 zł podstawowych potrzeb + 100 zł wymaganych minimalnych spłat + 100 zł dobrowolnej rezerwy; nieprzypisane: 0 zł. Spłaty policzono raz. pl.question: Co może pomóc poznać wydatki przed ułożeniem lub zmianą budżetu?

Nie odkładaj pilnych podstawowych potrzeb ani wymaganych minimalnych spłat na czas obserwacji. Wybierz wygodną metodę i wróć do niej, gdy możesz; nie trzeba przekazywać danych aplikacji.

pl.question: Masz w USA plan 401(k) z dopłatą pracodawcy. Jaki jest najmądrzejszy pierwszy ruch?

answers.text: Pominąć — dopłaty to podstęp
Wpłacać co najmniej tyle, by dostać pełną dopłatę pracodawcy (darmowe pieniądze)
Wpłacać dopiero po 60. roku życia
Wszystko w akcje jednej spółki

pl.explanation: Dopłata pracodawcy to natychmiastowy 100% zwrot z tych wpłat — zawsze wykorzystaj ją w całości.

pl.question: Co łączy brytyjskie ISA, japońskie NISA i polskie IKE?

answers.text: Gwarantują stały zysk 10%
To konta z ulgą podatkową, które chronią zyski z inwestycji
To rodzaje kart kredytowych
Są tylko dla milionerów

pl.explanation: ISA, NISA i IKE to opakowania podatkowe — pozwalają inwestycjom rosnąć bez zwykłego obciążenia podatkiem.

pl.question: Jaki cel inflacyjny ma bank centralny Indii (RBI)?

answers.text: 4% z pasmem tolerancji ±2 punkty procentowe
Nie ma celu

pl.explanation: RBI celuje w 4% inflacji z pasmem ±2 pkt proc. (2–6%), utrzymanym na lata 2026–2031.

pl.question: Jak rozumieć 50/30/20 jako elastyczną wskazówkę dla dochodu netto?

answers.text: 50% oszczędności, 30% potrzeby, 20% zachcianki
50% potrzeby, 30% zachcianki, 20% oszczędności i spłaty długu
Zawsze oszczędzać 20%, nawet kosztem podstawowych rachunków
Pożyczać, aby koniecznie odłożyć 20%

pl.explanation: 50/30/20 to orientacyjny podział dochodu netto, który można zmienić. Najpierw zabezpiecz podstawowe potrzeby i wymagane minimalne spłaty; nie licz tej samej spłaty dwukrotnie. Przy zmiennym dochodzie dostosuj kwoty. Bez nadwyżki nie wymuszaj oszczędzania 20%.

pl.question: Model: 1 000 zł, stałe hipotetyczne 5% rocznie, kapitalizacja roczna, odsetki zostają. Bez dopłat, wypłat, opłat i podatku; inflacja pominięta. Ile nominalnie po 2 latach?
pl.explanation: Procent składany nalicza odsetki także od zatrzymanych wcześniejszych odsetek. W modelu 1 000 × 1,05 × 1,05 = 1 102,50 zł. Dodatni wynik zależy od założonych 5%, nie samego czasu. To hipotetyczny rachunek, bez gwarancji rzeczywistego zysku; inwestycje mogą tracić.

pl.question: Co opisuje dywersyfikację i jej ograniczenie?

answers.text: Wszystko w jedną silną spółkę
Różne aktywa mogą ograniczyć koncentrację; straty nadal są możliwe
Jedna obligacja usuwa każde ryzyko
Częste transakcje gwarantują ochronę przed spadkiem

pl.explanation: Dywersyfikacja rozkłada ekspozycję na różne aktywa i może ograniczać ryzyko koncentracji. Nie usuwa ryzyka rynkowego ani nie gwarantuje uniknięcia strat. Różne nazwy funduszy mogą kryć podobne aktywa; sprawdź skład, ryzyko i koszty. Zakup nie jest wymagany.

pl.question: Jak działa lawina długu, gdy podstawowe potrzeby i wszystkie wymagane minimalne spłaty są zabezpieczone?

answers.text: Finansuje każdą nadpłatę nową pożyczką
Zawsze zaczyna od najmniejszego salda
Kieruje dostępną nadpłatę na dług o najwyższym oprocentowaniu
Pomija wymagane raty innych długów

pl.explanation: Lawina kieruje dostępną nadpłatę na najwyższe oprocentowanie po podstawowych potrzebach i minimach wszystkich długów. Przy stałych stopach i braku dodatkowych opłat może ograniczać odsetki. Sprawdź opłaty i skutki zaległości; bez nadwyżki nie wymuszaj nadpłaty. Nie gwarantuje najniższego łącznego kosztu w każdych warunkach.

pl.question: Hipotetycznie: nominalnie +2% i inflacja 5% za ten sam rok, bez opłat i podatku. Jaka jest realna stopa zwrotu po zaokrągleniu?

answers.text: Około −2,86%

pl.explanation: Dokładna relacja to (1,02 ÷1,05 −1) × 100% ≈ −2,86%. Odejmowanie 2% −5% =−3% jest przybliżeniem. Początkowe 1 000 zł daje nominalnie 1 020 zł, czyli około 971,43 zł w cenach początkowych. Model zakłada ten sam rok, brak opłat i podatku; nie opisuje bieżącej oferty.

pl.question: Które stwierdzenie o funduszach jest poprawne?

answers.text: Każdy ETF zawsze śledzi indeks
Fundusz indeksowy śledzi indeks; ETF może być indeksowy lub aktywny
Każdy fundusz indeksowy jest najtańszy
Każdy ETF gwarantuje wynik lepszy od rynku

pl.explanation: Fundusz indeksowy ma na celu śledzenie indeksu. ETF to forma funduszu notowanego na giełdzie; może być indeksowy lub aktywny. Żadna z tych nazw nie gwarantuje niskich kosztów, przewagi nad rynkiem ani braku strat. Sprawdź cel, skład, ryzyko i wszystkie koszty. Nie musisz inwestować.

pl.question: Co opisuje DCA?

answers.text: Kupowanie całej kwoty wyłącznie w najniższej cenie
Sprzedaż wszystkiego przy każdym spadku
Stała kwota w regularnych odstępach, niezależnie od ceny
Zamiana oszczędności na dolary

pl.explanation: DCA oznacza równą kwotę w regularnych odstępach; niższa cena daje więcej jednostek. Nie gwarantuje zysku ani ochrony przed stratą i nie usuwa automatycznie emocji.
