Buy luxury items before groceries

zh.explanation: First reserve money for essentials and required minimum payments, then choose savings from available surplus before discretionary spending. A transfer is optional; no surplus means no transfer, without blame.

zh.question: With PLN 4,000 take-home income, what is the illustrative 20% bucket?

answers.text: PLN 800

zh.explanation: 4,000 × 20% = PLN 800. In this example, required minimum debt payments are included once in needs; the 20% bucket is savings and extra debt repayment. This is our illustration convention, not a compulsory split.

zh.question: Which checklist is most complete when comparing savings accounts in Poland?

answers.text: Only the advertised interest rate
Rates and conditions, fees, access, and deposit protection
Whether the account guarantees an inflation-beating return
Whether your deposit is automatically invested in stocks

zh.explanation: Check the rate and its duration, qualifying conditions, fees, withdrawal access, and the applicable deposit guarantee scheme. A deposit account is not a stock investment; inflation can still reduce purchasing power.

zh.question: You invest PLN 100 twice, at PLN 10 then PLN 20 per unit. What do you buy?

answers.text: 10 units both times
5 units then 10 units
10 units then 5 units
A guaranteed profit

zh.explanation: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 units; 100 ÷ 20 = 5 units. DCA uses equal amounts at regular intervals, not equal unit counts. At PLN 8 per unit, all 15 units are worth PLN 120 against PLN 200 invested: a PLN 80 loss, ignoring fees and taxes.

zh.question: For one year, assumed nominal return is 2% and inflation 5%, with no fees, tax or cash flows. What is real return?

answers.text: Approximately −2.86%

zh.explanation: PLN 1,000 becomes PLN 1,020 nominally, but 1,020 ÷ 1.05 ≈ PLN 971.43 in starting prices. Real return is approximately −2.86%; 2% − 5% = −3% is only a subtraction estimate, with fees/tax and cash flows excluded.

zh.question: Assume a fixed 6% nominal rate, annual compounding and no fees, tax or cash flows. What does Rule of 72 estimate?

answers.text: 432 years, a guaranteed result
About 12 years to double, without a guarantee
0.08 years, a guaranteed result
Exactly 12 years even if rates change

zh.explanation: Rule of 72 estimates nominal doubling: 72 ÷ a positive annual percentage rate. At an assumed fixed 6% with annual compounding/reinvestment and no cash flows, fees or tax, this is about 12 years. It is not an exact result, forecast or guarantee; inflation is excluded here.

zh.question: Someone says an investment will always beat inflation. Which response is justified?

answers.text: Treat good past returns as a guarantee
Invest essential bill money to avoid inflation
Check loss risk, costs and access; gains are not guaranteed
A long holding period removes all loss risk

zh.explanation: No investment automatically guarantees beating inflation. Check possible loss, costs and access to money. Past results and a long holding period are not guarantees. Protect essentials and required minimum repayments; postponing investment is an option when income varies.

zh.question: After essentials and required minimums, PLN 100 remains. A PLN 1,000 debt charges 20% and a PLN 500 debt 10% annually; fixed rates, no fees, penalties or arrears. Where does avalanche direct the extra?

answers.text: Split equally, ignoring rates
To the smallest debt regardless of rate
To the debt charging 20%
Instead of another debt's minimum

zh.explanation: After essentials and all required minimums, avalanche directs the available extra PLN 100 to the higher 20% rate. This model assumes fixed rates and no fees, penalties or arrears; actual prepayment terms depend on the contract. No extra payment is required without a surplus.

zh.question: Which statement distinguishes BIK repayment history from repayment capacity in Poland?

answers.text: A high score guarantees a new loan
Timeliness matters; a lender also assesses income and expenses
Coachfi points replace a lender's assessment
Income does not matter for repayment capacity

zh.explanation: Timely repayment matters for risk assessment. A lender also assesses income, expenses and debts, then makes its own decision. A BIK score does not guarantee a loan; Coachfi points are not a BIK score. No new debt or paid report is needed for the exercise.

zh.question: You sell a fixed-cash-flow bond before maturity. Its required market yield rises, other factors unchanged. What happens to its price?

answers.text: It rises
It falls
The coupon automatically rises
Principal at maturity automatically falls

zh.explanation: For the same fixed cash flows, a higher required yield means a lower secondary-market price. This does not automatically change the coupon or contractual principal at maturity. Sale price, redemption terms and default risk are distinct; this is not a rule for every bond.

zh.question: Which decision conflicts with a readily accessible reserve with low volatility?

answers.text: Check access timing
Check fees and protection scope
Put the entire reserve in volatile shares
Distinguish reserves from planned spending

zh.explanation: An entire reserve in volatile shares may lose value when needed. Check access, fees and terms; lower risk does not mean no losses or costs. Deposit protection depends on the institution and product, and does not cover every investment. This is not a provider choice.

zh.question: Example: PLN 1,000 income, PLN 900 essentials, PLN 80 required minimums, no other costs or fees. Which small start fits these conditions?

answers.text: Transfer PLN 100 from a PLN 20 surplus
Optionally save PLN 10, leaving PLN 10
Borrow to save
Treat one month of costs as a required first threshold

zh.explanation: 1,000 − 900 − 80 = PLN 20. An optional PLN 10 fits the surplus and leaves PLN 10; no transfer is required. At PLN 980 income, surplus is PLN 0. One month of expenses is not a required first goal; without funds, pause the transfer and do not borrow to save.

zh.question: What is compound interest when credited interest stays in the balance?

answers.text: Interest only on the initial amount
An early withdrawal fee
Interest on principal and retained earlier interest
A certain profit from every investment

zh.explanation: In a hypothetical model, PLN 1,000 at a constant 5% a year with annual compounding becomes PLN 1,050, then PLN 1,102.50. Interest stays; there are no contributions, withdrawals, fees or tax, and inflation is ignored. The extra PLN 2.50 is interest on the first PLN 50 of interest. This is a nominal model, not an offer or guaranteed investment profit.

zh.question: What is the purpose of diversification, without guaranteeing no losses?

answers.text: Putting everything into one company
Spreading investments to reduce concentration risk
Ensuring a profit regardless of the market
Changing the portfolio weekly to ensure a profit

zh.explanation: Different investments can reduce dependence on one issuer or sector. Multiple holdings may still share risks and fall together. Diversification does not guarantee profit or remove the risk of market losses.

zh.question: What defines an index fund?

answers.text: Always having zero costs
An objective of tracking a specified index
Every ETF being an index fund
A guaranteed return above the market

zh.explanation: An index fund seeks to track a specified index. Costs and tracking error can create differences in returns. Not every index fund is cheaper; check actual costs and risks. An ETF may track an index or be actively managed. The name does not promise market outperformance.

zh.question: What does ETF mean?

answers.text: An account with guaranteed interest
A bank transfer fee
A fund whose shares trade on an exchange
A fund that always tracks a broad index

zh.explanation: An ETF is an exchange-traded fund. It may follow an index or an active strategy and hold a narrow set of investments. An ETF alone does not ensure broad diversification or protect capital. Check holdings, risks, fees and buying and selling costs; losses are possible.

zh.question: What belongs in an investment plan instead of assuming time alone guarantees profit?

answers.text: The date of a certain market bottom
Goals, horizon, reserves, acceptable losses and costs
Always selling after a 10% drop
Always holding every investment

zh.explanation: A long horizon alone does not guarantee profit. A plan depends on goals, when money is needed, reserves, risk and costs; it can be reassessed when circumstances change. This is not an always-hold or sell-after-a-set-drop rule. Essentials and required minimums come first, and without surplus it is acceptable not to invest.

zh.question: What is the purpose of planning finances for retirement?

answers.text: Certainty of maintaining every current income
Preparing resources for future needs after work changes or ends
Replacing emergency reserves with a risky investment
Doubling money simply by opening an account

zh.explanation: A plan compares future needs and possible sources of funds; it does not guarantee maintaining current income. Emergency reserves have a separate role. Outcomes depend on contributions, conditions, costs and risk, among other factors. Essentials, required minimum repayments and reserves come first; without surplus, start with a free planning exercise, without buying anything or opening an account.

zh.question: Model: PLN 1,000 once, a constant 5% a year, annual compounding, interest retained. No later contributions, withdrawals, fees or tax; inflation ignored. What is the nominal balance after 2 years?
zh.explanation: In this hypothetical model, 1,000 × 1.05 × 1.05 = PLN 1,102.50. After year one the balance is PLN 1,050; the second interest payment is PLN 52.50. The positive result comes from the assumed constant rate, not time alone. More periods allow more compounding here, but actual outcomes can differ and losses are possible. This is not a pension forecast or a recommendation to contribute.

zh.question: What can a survey percentage of correct answers about compound interest in Poland tell us?

answers.text: Everyone answering incorrectly will fall into debt
Knowledge alone guarantees a high pension
It is a result of specific questions, sample, year and scoring
That percentage describes all financial behaviour

zh.explanation: Check the year, surveyed population, questions and scoring method. A knowledge result is not the same as behaviour or financial circumstances. A statistical association alone does not prove that lacking this knowledge directly causes debt or low retirement savings.

zh.question: Does a survey percentage of stated trust establish that a particular institution is safe?

answers.text: Yes, if it has many customers
Yes, every higher percentage means no risk
Yes, if the result is older
No; a survey does not replace checking the institution

zh.explanation: Check the date, sample and exact wording, including whether the question concerns institutions or their employees. Stated trust does not certify a particular institution or product as safe. A percentage alone also does not prove a cause of savings or wealth.

zh.question: How should a gap to the maximum financial-literacy survey score be interpreted?

answers.text: As a certain amount of lost savings
As a point gap dependent on questions and scoring
As a future investment return
As proof that the respondent is to blame

zh.explanation: Check the year, sample, instrument version and scoring key. A historical result does not automatically describe the current population. A point gap does not measure lost wealth and alone proves neither behaviour nor causes of financial difficulties.

zh.question: What should be established before comparing PPK and PPE participation percentages?

answers.text: Only the highest percentage
That both names mean the same programme
The separate programme, date and group used for each percentage
That non-participation proves a lack of knowledge

zh.explanation: PPK and PPE are separate arrangements. Identify the programme, date, surveyed group and denominator; do not combine percentages without a stated method. Participation statistics alone explain neither why people decide nor whether a lack of compound-interest knowledge caused that decision.

zh.question: Which set most fully describes financial well-being in the CFPB framework?

answers.text: Only income level
Day-to-day finances, shock absorption, goals and freedom of choice
Only a financial quiz score
The number of financial products owned

zh.explanation: The CFPB framework covers a sense of control over current finances, capacity to handle shocks, progress towards goals and freedom of choice. It is a descriptive framework, not a guarantee after mastering three tasks. Resources, circumstances and personal perceptions also matter; not everything depends on individual choices.

zh.question: What best describes financial resilience?

answers.text: A guaranteed million in savings
An absolute absence of any debt
The capacity to handle a financial shock and rebuild one’s situation
Merely having an insurance policy

zh.explanation: Income, resources, obligations, available support and the size of a shock matter, not just knowledge or mindset. A reserve may help but guarantees no coverage of every expense. Choose contributions voluntarily after essential needs and required minimum repayments; without a surplus, pause contributions.

zh.question: Exercise: PLN 1000 debt, a hypothetical fixed 10% per period added to the debt. For 2 periods there are no repayments, fees or new borrowing. What is the balance?

answers.text: PLN 1000
PLN 1210
PLN 1200
PLN 2000

zh.explanation: 1000 × 1.10 × 1.10 = PLN 1210. This is an assumed model, not an offer or a rule for every contract. Actual cost depends on terms and repayments. Debt difficulties can also involve lost income, unexpected costs and fees. A quiz establishes neither the cause of difficulties nor a person’s blame.

zh.question: What is the main purpose of life insurance?

answers.text: To get rich when someone dies
To replace income for dependents if the primary earner dies
To save on taxes
To invest in the stock market safely

zh.explanation: Life insurance protects dependents by replacing the primary earner's income if they die prematurely.

zh.question: What is the recommended approach to finances for couples?

answers.text: One partner handles all finances, the other doesn't need to know
Both partners should understand the full financial picture and plan together
Keep all finances 100% separate — never share anything
Whoever earns more controls all decisions

zh.explanation: Financial transparency and joint planning between partners leads to better decisions and fewer conflicts.

zh.question: What is the most effective way to teach kids about money?

answers.text: Give them pocket money with no conditions
Let them observe — never discuss money with children
Give pocket money with saving rules (e.g. save 20%, spend 60%, give 20%)
Wait until they're 18 to discuss finances

zh.explanation: Pocket money with saving/spending rules gives kids real financial decisions at low cost.

zh.question: What inflation rate has the National Bank of Poland (NBP) targeted since 2004?

answers.text: 0% — prices should never rise
2.5% with a ±1 percentage point band
5% to encourage spending
Whatever the government sets each year

zh.explanation: Since 2004 the NBP's target is 2.5% (±1 percentage point), measured by the annual change in the CPI.

zh.question: Why do central banks aim for low, positive inflation (~2–2.5%) instead of 0%?

answers.text: To make the currency worthless faster
A small, stable buffer supports growth and avoids dangerous deflation
Because higher prices are always good
To increase government tax revenue only

zh.explanation: A low, stable target avoids deflation (which can stall an economy) and keeps inflation predictable.

zh.question: What is a central bank's main tool for steering inflation?

answers.text: Printing more banknotes for citizens
Setting benchmark interest rates
Fixing the price of bread
Banning imports

zh.explanation: Central banks mainly use benchmark interest rates to influence borrowing, demand and ultimately inflation.

zh.question: When a central bank raises interest rates, what typically happens?

answers.text: Borrowing gets cheaper and spending jumps
Borrowing gets more expensive, cooling demand and inflation
Nothing changes for households
Savings accounts always pay 0%

zh.explanation: Rate hikes raise the cost of borrowing, which cools spending and helps bring inflation down.

zh.question: What does GDP (Gross Domestic Product) measure?

answers.text: The total savings of all citizens
The value of all goods and services produced in an economy
The amount of cash in circulation
The national debt

zh.explanation: GDP = the total market value of goods and services produced in a country over a period.

zh.question: Why is persistent deflation (falling prices) considered dangerous?

answers.text: It makes everyone richer with no downside
People delay purchases, demand drops, and debts get harder to repay
It always boosts wages
It has no effect on the economy

zh.explanation: Deflation pushes people to delay spending and makes existing debt heavier in real terms — a dangerous loop.

zh.question: What does “zero” mean in zero-based budgeting?

answers.text: You must spend everything and empty the account
Every available unit has a purpose in the plan, including reserves
Savings must equal zero
Only cash may be used

zh.explanation: This is a planning method, not a requirement to spend everything or empty an account. Hypothetically: PLN 1000 = 800 for essential needs + 100 for required minimum repayments + 100 for a voluntary reserve; unallocated: PLN 0. Repayments are counted once. Update the plan when income varies; no surplus means no duty to save. The plan does not guarantee freedom from unexpected expenses.

zh.question: What can help you understand spending before making or revising a budget?

answers.text: First postpone urgent essential purchases for 30 days
Optionally review your own spending over a suitable period using a method you choose
Everyone must first collect exactly 30 days of data
Borrow money instead of checking spending

zh.explanation: You can start with a day or week of your own notes and extend the period; 30 days is not a mandatory prerequisite. Include less frequent bills and variable income too. Do not postpone urgent essential needs or required minimum repayments while observing. Choose a manageable method and return when you can; you do not need to share data with the app.

zh.question: You have PLN 0 saved for an optional PLN 600 purchase in 6 months. What are 6 equal monthly contributions before purchase, ignoring interest and fees?

answers.text: PLN 600 each month
PLN 100 each month for this planned goal
PLN 0, because reserves guarantee every cost is covered
Borrowing always replaces such a plan

zh.explanation: 600 ÷ 6 = PLN 100 monthly in this hypothetical plan. A sinking fund is for a known future cost; emergency reserves cover unexpected events. Contributions are voluntary, after essential needs and required minimum repayments. With no surplus, change the goal or postpone this optional purchase; update the plan when income varies. There is no guarantee of avoiding debt.

zh.question: What could you optionally do before a non-urgent, non-essential purchase?

answers.text: Always buy immediately and check the cost later
Take a pause you choose and check the need, price and plan
Postpone urgent essential purchases too
Assume every pause guarantees savings

zh.explanation: You can pause and return to the decision at a suitable time. This is an option, not a mandatory 24 hours or a guarantee of savings or a change in desire to buy. Do not postpone urgent essential needs or required minimum repayments. After a break, calmly check the price, available money and priorities; you can revise the decision without pressure.

zh.question: After covering essentials and all required minimum repayments, PLN 20 remains. Which small first step is an optional choice in this example?

answers.text: Save a full month of costs at once as a requirement
Choose e.g. PLN 5; pause if there is no surplus
Borrow PLN 100 to start a reserve
Transfer all income before paying bills

zh.explanation: Example budget: PLN 1,200 income − PLN 1,080 essentials − PLN 100 required minimums = PLN 20 surplus, with no other costs or fees. An optional PLN 5 leaves PLN 15; no transfer is required. Adapt the goal to circumstances without requiring a full month at the start. Without surplus, pause; do not borrow to save.

zh.question: In Poland, up to what amount are bank deposits guaranteed by the BFG?

answers.text: There is no deposit guarantee
The PLN equivalent of €100,000 per depositor, per bank
Exactly 10,000 PLN total
Unlimited, always 100%

zh.question: What is the general relationship between risk and expected return?

answers.text: Higher expected returns generally come with higher risk
High returns are guaranteed with zero risk
Risk and return are unrelated
Lower risk always means higher return

zh.explanation: Higher potential return generally requires taking on more risk. Be sceptical of 'high return, no risk' offers.

zh.question: How should beginners treat highly speculative assets like crypto?

answers.text: Put all savings in for maximum gains
Limit to a small share you could afford to lose entirely
Borrow money to buy more
Treat it as a safe emergency fund

zh.explanation: Keep speculative assets to a small portion of your portfolio, and only money you can afford to lose completely.

zh.question: What's the key tax difference between Poland's IKE and IKZE accounts?

IKE: tax-free gains on a qualifying withdrawal; IKZE: deduct contributions now, pay a 10% flat tax on withdrawal
Both are taxed at 19% every year
Neither offers any tax benefit

zh.question: In Poland's PPK, what does the employer add on top of the employee's 2% basic contribution?

A flat 100 PLN regardless of salary

zh.question: What state incentives does Poland's PPK give participants?

Free shares in the employer

zh.question: What do deposit guarantee schemes (BFG, FDIC, EU DGS, FGC) actually protect?

answers.text: All investments including stocks and crypto
Bank deposits — not stocks, funds, pensions or crypto
Only cash kept at home
Your salary if you lose your job

zh.question: In the United States, how much does the FDIC insure per depositor, per bank?

Unlimited

zh.question: Across the EU (incl. Poland, Spain, France), bank deposits are guaranteed up to…

€100,000 per depositor, per bank (or local-currency equivalent)
Nothing is guaranteed in the EU

zh.explanation: EU rules harmonise deposit protection at €100,000 per depositor, per bank.

zh.question: With a US 401(k) that offers an employer match, what's the smartest first move?

answers.text: Skip it — matches are a trick
Contribute at least enough to get the full employer match (free money)
Only contribute after age 60
Put it all into a single company stock

zh.explanation: Always contribute enough to capture the full employer match — it's free money you can't get any other way.

zh.question: What do a UK ISA, a Japanese NISA and a Polish IKE have in common?

answers.text: They guarantee a fixed 10% return
They are tax-advantaged accounts that shelter investment growth
They are types of credit card
They are only for millionaires

zh.explanation: ISA (UK), NISA (Japan) and IKE (Poland) are tax-advantaged accounts that shelter investment gains.

zh.question: What inflation target does India's central bank (RBI) aim for?

answers.text: 4% with a ±2 percentage point tolerance band
It has no target

zh.explanation: India's RBI targets 4% inflation with a tolerance band of ±2 percentage points (2–6%).

zh.question: 什么是 50/30/20 预算法则？
zh.explanation: 50% 用于必需开支（房租、食物），30% 用于想要的东西（娱乐），20% 用于储蓄和还债。简单而有效。

zh.question: 什么是复利？

answers.text: 只按本金支付的利息
提前支取的银行手续费
在本金和已获得的利息上共同赚取的利息
只有信用卡才需要支付的利息

zh.explanation: 复利意味着利息也会产生利息，随着时间推移形成指数级增长。据说爱因斯坦称它为世界第八大奇迹。

zh.question: 投资中的“分散”是什么意思？

answers.text: 把所有钱投入一只强势股票
把投资分散到不同资产上以降低风险
只投资国债
每周更换投资组合

zh.explanation: 不要把所有鸡蛋放在一个篮子里。分散投资能降低一次糟糕的投资毁掉整个组合的风险。

zh.question: 什么是“债务雪崩”策略？

answers.text: 借新贷还旧贷
不管利率，先还最小的债务
先还利率最高的债务，把总利息降到最低
不理会债务，任其增长

zh.explanation: 债务雪崩 = 先攻克利率最高的债务。从数学上讲这最省钱。与之相对的“债务雪球”则是先还最小的欠款来获得动力。

zh.question: 如果通胀是 5%，银行给 2%，你的储蓄实际回报是多少？
zh.explanation: 实际回报 = 名义利率 − 通胀 = 2% − 5% = −3%。即使存在 2% 的储蓄账户里，你的钱也在失去购买力。

zh.question: 哪种基金以低费用自动跟踪市场指数？

answers.text: 对冲基金
指数基金 / ETF
风险投资基金
养老基金

zh.explanation: 指数基金和 ETF 被动跟踪市场指数（如标普 500）。它们费用很低，历史上跑赢了大多数主动管理基金。

zh.question: 什么是定期定额投资（DCA）？

answers.text: 在市场最低点全部买入
价格下跌时全部卖出
无论价格如何，按固定周期投入固定金额
把所有储蓄换成美元

zh.explanation: 定期定额就是每个月投入相同的固定金额，不管价格如何。价格低时买得多，价格高时买得少，把情绪从投资中剔除。

zh.question: 什么是“72 法则”？

answers.text: 还清任何债务都需要 72 个月
用 72 除以年回报率，估算多少年能让钱翻倍
把收入的 72% 存起来
72 岁退休以获得最高养老金

zh.explanation: 72 ÷ 年回报率 = 钱翻倍所需的年数。回报率 8% 时大约 9 年翻倍，6% 时大约 12 年。一个快速的心算技巧。

zh.question: 什么是 ETF？

answers.text: 利息更高的储蓄账户
电子转账手续费
交易所交易基金：一篮子像股票一样交易的资产
政府的应急基金

zh.explanation: ETF 把许多资产（股票、债券、大宗商品）打包成一个可交易的工具。它兼具基金的分散性和股票的灵活性。

zh.question: 以下哪一项不是好的应急基金的特点？

answers.text: 容易取用（流动性强）
覆盖 3–6 个月的开支
投资于高风险股票以追求最大增长
与日常消费账户分开存放

zh.explanation: 应急基金应当流动且安全，而不是投资于波动大的资产。它的作用是在紧急情况发生时可以取用，而不是增值。

zh.question: 利率上升时，债券价格会怎样？

answers.text: 债券价格上涨
债券价格下跌
没有变化
债券价格翻倍

zh.explanation: 债券和利率反向变动。利率上升时，利率较低的现有债券吸引力下降，因此市场价格下跌。

zh.question: 什么是“生活方式膨胀”？

answers.text: 政府提高最低工资
物价涨得比工资快
赚得越多花得越多，储蓄却没有增加
在简历上夸大自己的生活方式

zh.explanation: 生活方式膨胀意味着每次加薪都被新的开销吃掉。解药是：在习惯这笔额外收入之前，先把加薪存起来。

zh.question: 养老金/退休账户的主要目的是什么？

answers.text: 支付度假费用
利用几十年的复利，在你停止工作后替代收入
投机高风险资产
存放应急现金

zh.explanation: 退休账户是长期工具。投入的资金在几十年里享受税收优惠地增长。时间是你最大的资产：25 岁开始比 35 岁开始，最终余额可能相差一倍。

zh.question: “净资产”是什么意思？

answers.text: 你的税后月薪
总资产减去总负债
你钱包里有多少现金
你的信用评分

zh.explanation: 净资产 = 你拥有的一切（资产）减去你欠下的一切（负债）。持续增长的正净资产才是财务健康的真正衡量标准，比收入本身更有意义。

zh.question: 根据经合组织的数据，有多少比例的波兰人正确理解复利？
zh.explanation: 实际上只有约三分之一的波兰人理解复利。这是头号知识缺口：它会导致债务螺旋，也解释了为什么只有 47% 的员工加入自愿性的 PPK/PPE 养老金计划。

zh.question: 2022 年有多少比例的波兰人在储蓄方面信任金融机构？
zh.explanation: 2022 年只有 15% 的波兰人信任金融机构，而 2021 年曾跌到仅 6%。这种信任赤字是参与金融活动和长期积累财富的一大障碍。

zh.question: 波兰在经合组织金融能力评估中得了 13/21。缺失的分数代表什么？

answers.text: 没什么要紧：13/21 已经很优秀
错失的财富积累机会和财务准备的不足
经合组织测试中的语言障碍
银行账户持有率低

zh.explanation: 13/21 让波兰处于中游。缺失的 8 分代表实实在在错失的机会：资本市场利用效率较低、应急基金比例较低，以及更容易受到经济冲击。

zh.question: 近一半的波兰人表示财务在掌控他们的生活。建议怎样转变心态？

answers.text: 不惜一切代价多赚钱
为了减压而避免去想钱
重建个人掌控感：把钱当作工具，而不是压力来源
把一切都交给理财顾问

zh.explanation: 当人们感到无法掌控时，短期思维是一种心理防御。财商教育必须恢复这种掌控感，把钱从压力来源变成赋能的工具。

zh.question: 哪个波兰语概念描述的是应急的财务缓冲？

answers.text: Kapitał własny
Poduszka finansowa
Rezerwa walutowa
Dywidenda bezpieczeństwa

zh.explanation: “Poduszka finansowa”（财务垫子）是波兰语中对应急基金的说法。它是财务健康的核心组成部分：提供一张安全网，在不借高息贷款的情况下吸收意外冲击。

zh.question: 经合组织发现，只有 26.9% 的波兰人达到金融态度的最低目标分。“金融态度”衡量的是什么？

answers.text: 一个人拥有多少金融产品
收入水平和储蓄率
一个人是为未来做规划，还是只活在当下
对银行的信任程度

zh.explanation: 金融态度衡量的是倾向于规划未来，还是只考虑眼前。波兰 26.9% 的达标率大约是经合组织平均水平的一半，反映出一种普遍的短期财务思维文化。

ja.question: インフレとは何ですか？

answers.text: 時間とともにお金で買えるものが増える
時間とともにお金の購買力が下がる
銀行がお金を無料で配る
価格は常に下がる

ja.explanation: インフレとは、同じ金額で買えるものが時間とともに減ることです。

ja.question: 緊急資金は何か月分の支出をカバーすべきですか？

answers.text: 1 週間
1 か月
3 から 6 か月

ja.explanation: 実用的な緊急資金は通常、3 から 6 か月分の必要支出をカバーします。

ja.question: 最も効果的な貯蓄習慣はどれですか？

answers.text: 月末に残った分だけ貯める
収入が増えた時だけ貯める
給料後に固定額を自動で移す
すべて現金で家に置く

ja.explanation: 最も効果的なのは、収入が入った直後の自動振替です。

ja.question: 金利が上がると変動金利ローンは通常どうなりますか？

answers.text: 月々の支払いが下がる
何も変わらない
月々の支払いが上がりやすい
ローンが消える

ja.explanation: 変動金利ローンは市場金利に連動するため、支払いが増えることがあります。

ja.question: What is 'net worth'?

answers.text: Your monthly salary after tax
Total assets minus total liabilities
How much cash you have in your wallet
Your credit score

ja.explanation: Net worth is assets minus liabilities at the same date. Income is a flow; cash and credit scores are different measures. Net worth alone does not describe liquidity or your value as a person.

ja.question: What is 'lifestyle inflation'?

answers.text: Government increasing minimum wage
Prices rising faster than salaries
Choosing more discretionary spending as your income rises
Inflating your lifestyle on your resume

ja.explanation: Lifestyle inflation is a voluntary rise in discretionary spending as income grows. It is different from price inflation or necessary expenses, and it does not mean every raise is fully spent.

ja.question: What does 'pay yourself first' mean?

answers.text: Spend on yourself before paying bills
Plan affordable savings after reserving money for essentials and required minimum payments
Increase your own salary first
Buy luxury items before groceries

ja.explanation: First reserve money for essentials and required minimum payments, then choose savings from available surplus before discretionary spending. A transfer is optional; no surplus means no transfer, without blame.

ja.question: With PLN 4,000 take-home income, what is the illustrative 20% bucket?

answers.text: PLN 800

ja.explanation: 4,000 × 20% = PLN 800. In this example, required minimum debt payments are included once in needs; the 20% bucket is savings and extra debt repayment. This is our illustration convention, not a compulsory split.

ja.question: Which checklist is most complete when comparing savings accounts in Poland?

answers.text: Only the advertised interest rate
Rates and conditions, fees, access, and deposit protection
Whether the account guarantees an inflation-beating return
Whether your deposit is automatically invested in stocks

ja.explanation: Check the rate and its duration, qualifying conditions, fees, withdrawal access, and the applicable deposit guarantee scheme. A deposit account is not a stock investment; inflation can still reduce purchasing power.

ja.question: You invest PLN 100 twice, at PLN 10 then PLN 20 per unit. What do you buy?

answers.text: 10 units both times
5 units then 10 units
10 units then 5 units
A guaranteed profit

ja.explanation: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 units; 100 ÷ 20 = 5 units. DCA uses equal amounts at regular intervals, not equal unit counts. At PLN 8 per unit, all 15 units are worth PLN 120 against PLN 200 invested: a PLN 80 loss, ignoring fees and taxes.

ja.question: For one year, assumed nominal return is 2% and inflation 5%, with no fees, tax or cash flows. What is real return?

answers.text: Approximately −2.86%

ja.explanation: PLN 1,000 becomes PLN 1,020 nominally, but 1,020 ÷ 1.05 ≈ PLN 971.43 in starting prices. Real return is approximately −2.86%; 2% − 5% = −3% is only a subtraction estimate, with fees/tax and cash flows excluded.

ja.question: Assume a fixed 6% nominal rate, annual compounding and no fees, tax or cash flows. What does Rule of 72 estimate?

answers.text: 432 years, a guaranteed result
About 12 years to double, without a guarantee
0.08 years, a guaranteed result
Exactly 12 years even if rates change

ja.explanation: Rule of 72 estimates nominal doubling: 72 ÷ a positive annual percentage rate. At an assumed fixed 6% with annual compounding/reinvestment and no cash flows, fees or tax, this is about 12 years. It is not an exact result, forecast or guarantee; inflation is excluded here.

ja.question: Someone says an investment will always beat inflation. Which response is justified?

answers.text: Treat good past returns as a guarantee
Invest essential bill money to avoid inflation
Check loss risk, costs and access; gains are not guaranteed
A long holding period removes all loss risk

ja.explanation: No investment automatically guarantees beating inflation. Check possible loss, costs and access to money. Past results and a long holding period are not guarantees. Protect essentials and required minimum repayments; postponing investment is an option when income varies.

ja.question: After essentials and required minimums, PLN 100 remains. A PLN 1,000 debt charges 20% and a PLN 500 debt 10% annually; fixed rates, no fees, penalties or arrears. Where does avalanche direct the extra?

answers.text: Split equally, ignoring rates
To the smallest debt regardless of rate
To the debt charging 20%
Instead of another debt's minimum

ja.explanation: After essentials and all required minimums, avalanche directs the available extra PLN 100 to the higher 20% rate. This model assumes fixed rates and no fees, penalties or arrears; actual prepayment terms depend on the contract. No extra payment is required without a surplus.

ja.question: Which statement distinguishes BIK repayment history from repayment capacity in Poland?

answers.text: A high score guarantees a new loan
Timeliness matters; a lender also assesses income and expenses
Coachfi points replace a lender's assessment
Income does not matter for repayment capacity

ja.explanation: Timely repayment matters for risk assessment. A lender also assesses income, expenses and debts, then makes its own decision. A BIK score does not guarantee a loan; Coachfi points are not a BIK score. No new debt or paid report is needed for the exercise.

ja.question: You sell a fixed-cash-flow bond before maturity. Its required market yield rises, other factors unchanged. What happens to its price?

answers.text: It rises
It falls
The coupon automatically rises
Principal at maturity automatically falls

ja.explanation: For the same fixed cash flows, a higher required yield means a lower secondary-market price. This does not automatically change the coupon or contractual principal at maturity. Sale price, redemption terms and default risk are distinct; this is not a rule for every bond.

ja.question: Which decision conflicts with a readily accessible reserve with low volatility?

answers.text: Check access timing
Check fees and protection scope
Put the entire reserve in volatile shares
Distinguish reserves from planned spending

ja.explanation: An entire reserve in volatile shares may lose value when needed. Check access, fees and terms; lower risk does not mean no losses or costs. Deposit protection depends on the institution and product, and does not cover every investment. This is not a provider choice.

ja.question: Example: PLN 1,000 income, PLN 900 essentials, PLN 80 required minimums, no other costs or fees. Which small start fits these conditions?

answers.text: Transfer PLN 100 from a PLN 20 surplus
Optionally save PLN 10, leaving PLN 10
Borrow to save
Treat one month of costs as a required first threshold

ja.explanation: 1,000 − 900 − 80 = PLN 20. An optional PLN 10 fits the surplus and leaves PLN 10; no transfer is required. At PLN 980 income, surplus is PLN 0. One month of expenses is not a required first goal; without funds, pause the transfer and do not borrow to save.

ja.question: What is compound interest when credited interest stays in the balance?

answers.text: Interest only on the initial amount
An early withdrawal fee
Interest on principal and retained earlier interest
A certain profit from every investment

ja.explanation: In a hypothetical model, PLN 1,000 at a constant 5% a year with annual compounding becomes PLN 1,050, then PLN 1,102.50. Interest stays; there are no contributions, withdrawals, fees or tax, and inflation is ignored. The extra PLN 2.50 is interest on the first PLN 50 of interest. This is a nominal model, not an offer or guaranteed investment profit.

ja.question: What is the purpose of diversification, without guaranteeing no losses?

answers.text: Putting everything into one company
Spreading investments to reduce concentration risk
Ensuring a profit regardless of the market
Changing the portfolio weekly to ensure a profit

ja.explanation: Different investments can reduce dependence on one issuer or sector. Multiple holdings may still share risks and fall together. Diversification does not guarantee profit or remove the risk of market losses.

ja.question: What defines an index fund?

answers.text: Always having zero costs
An objective of tracking a specified index
Every ETF being an index fund
A guaranteed return above the market

ja.explanation: An index fund seeks to track a specified index. Costs and tracking error can create differences in returns. Not every index fund is cheaper; check actual costs and risks. An ETF may track an index or be actively managed. The name does not promise market outperformance.

ja.question: What does ETF mean?

answers.text: An account with guaranteed interest
A bank transfer fee
A fund whose shares trade on an exchange
A fund that always tracks a broad index

ja.explanation: An ETF is an exchange-traded fund. It may follow an index or an active strategy and hold a narrow set of investments. An ETF alone does not ensure broad diversification or protect capital. Check holdings, risks, fees and buying and selling costs; losses are possible.

ja.question: What belongs in an investment plan instead of assuming time alone guarantees profit?

answers.text: The date of a certain market bottom
Goals, horizon, reserves, acceptable losses and costs
Always selling after a 10% drop
Always holding every investment

ja.explanation: A long horizon alone does not guarantee profit. A plan depends on goals, when money is needed, reserves, risk and costs; it can be reassessed when circumstances change. This is not an always-hold or sell-after-a-set-drop rule. Essentials and required minimums come first, and without surplus it is acceptable not to invest.

ja.question: What is the purpose of planning finances for retirement?

answers.text: Certainty of maintaining every current income
Preparing resources for future needs after work changes or ends
Replacing emergency reserves with a risky investment
Doubling money simply by opening an account

ja.explanation: A plan compares future needs and possible sources of funds; it does not guarantee maintaining current income. Emergency reserves have a separate role. Outcomes depend on contributions, conditions, costs and risk, among other factors. Essentials, required minimum repayments and reserves come first; without surplus, start with a free planning exercise, without buying anything or opening an account.

ja.question: Model: PLN 1,000 once, a constant 5% a year, annual compounding, interest retained. No later contributions, withdrawals, fees or tax; inflation ignored. What is the nominal balance after 2 years?
ja.explanation: In this hypothetical model, 1,000 × 1.05 × 1.05 = PLN 1,102.50. After year one the balance is PLN 1,050; the second interest payment is PLN 52.50. The positive result comes from the assumed constant rate, not time alone. More periods allow more compounding here, but actual outcomes can differ and losses are possible. This is not a pension forecast or a recommendation to contribute.

ja.question: What can a survey percentage of correct answers about compound interest in Poland tell us?

answers.text: Everyone answering incorrectly will fall into debt
Knowledge alone guarantees a high pension
It is a result of specific questions, sample, year and scoring
That percentage describes all financial behaviour

ja.explanation: Check the year, surveyed population, questions and scoring method. A knowledge result is not the same as behaviour or financial circumstances. A statistical association alone does not prove that lacking this knowledge directly causes debt or low retirement savings.

ja.question: Does a survey percentage of stated trust establish that a particular institution is safe?

answers.text: Yes, if it has many customers
Yes, every higher percentage means no risk
Yes, if the result is older
No; a survey does not replace checking the institution

ja.explanation: Check the date, sample and exact wording, including whether the question concerns institutions or their employees. Stated trust does not certify a particular institution or product as safe. A percentage alone also does not prove a cause of savings or wealth.

ja.question: How should a gap to the maximum financial-literacy survey score be interpreted?

answers.text: As a certain amount of lost savings
As a point gap dependent on questions and scoring
As a future investment return
As proof that the respondent is to blame

ja.explanation: Check the year, sample, instrument version and scoring key. A historical result does not automatically describe the current population. A point gap does not measure lost wealth and alone proves neither behaviour nor causes of financial difficulties.

ja.question: What should be established before comparing PPK and PPE participation percentages?

answers.text: Only the highest percentage
That both names mean the same programme
The separate programme, date and group used for each percentage
That non-participation proves a lack of knowledge

ja.explanation: PPK and PPE are separate arrangements. Identify the programme, date, surveyed group and denominator; do not combine percentages without a stated method. Participation statistics alone explain neither why people decide nor whether a lack of compound-interest knowledge caused that decision.

ja.question: Which set most fully describes financial well-being in the CFPB framework?

answers.text: Only income level
Day-to-day finances, shock absorption, goals and freedom of choice
Only a financial quiz score
The number of financial products owned

ja.explanation: The CFPB framework covers a sense of control over current finances, capacity to handle shocks, progress towards goals and freedom of choice. It is a descriptive framework, not a guarantee after mastering three tasks. Resources, circumstances and personal perceptions also matter; not everything depends on individual choices.

ja.question: What best describes financial resilience?

answers.text: A guaranteed million in savings
An absolute absence of any debt
The capacity to handle a financial shock and rebuild one’s situation
Merely having an insurance policy

ja.explanation: Income, resources, obligations, available support and the size of a shock matter, not just knowledge or mindset. A reserve may help but guarantees no coverage of every expense. Choose contributions voluntarily after essential needs and required minimum repayments; without a surplus, pause contributions.

ja.question: Exercise: PLN 1000 debt, a hypothetical fixed 10% per period added to the debt. For 2 periods there are no repayments, fees or new borrowing. What is the balance?

answers.text: PLN 1000
PLN 1210
PLN 1200
PLN 2000

ja.explanation: 1000 × 1.10 × 1.10 = PLN 1210. This is an assumed model, not an offer or a rule for every contract. Actual cost depends on terms and repayments. Debt difficulties can also involve lost income, unexpected costs and fees. A quiz establishes neither the cause of difficulties nor a person’s blame.

ja.question: What is the main purpose of life insurance?

answers.text: To get rich when someone dies
To replace income for dependents if the primary earner dies
To save on taxes
To invest in the stock market safely

ja.explanation: Life insurance protects dependents by replacing the primary earner's income if they die prematurely.

ja.question: What is the recommended approach to finances for couples?

answers.text: One partner handles all finances, the other doesn't need to know
Both partners should understand the full financial picture and plan together
Keep all finances 100% separate — never share anything
Whoever earns more controls all decisions

ja.explanation: Financial transparency and joint planning between partners leads to better decisions and fewer conflicts.

ja.question: What is the most effective way to teach kids about money?

answers.text: Give them pocket money with no conditions
Let them observe — never discuss money with children
Give pocket money with saving rules (e.g. save 20%, spend 60%, give 20%)
Wait until they're 18 to discuss finances

ja.explanation: Pocket money with saving/spending rules gives kids real financial decisions at low cost.

ja.question: What inflation rate has the National Bank of Poland (NBP) targeted since 2004?

answers.text: 0% — prices should never rise
2.5% with a ±1 percentage point band
5% to encourage spending
Whatever the government sets each year

ja.explanation: Since 2004 the NBP's target is 2.5% (±1 percentage point), measured by the annual change in the CPI.

ja.question: Why do central banks aim for low, positive inflation (~2–2.5%) instead of 0%?

answers.text: To make the currency worthless faster
A small, stable buffer supports growth and avoids dangerous deflation
Because higher prices are always good
To increase government tax revenue only

ja.explanation: A low, stable target avoids deflation (which can stall an economy) and keeps inflation predictable.

ja.question: What is a central bank's main tool for steering inflation?

Setting benchmark interest rates
Fixing the price of bread
Banning imports

Borrowing gets more expensive, cooling demand and inflation
Nothing changes for households
Savings accounts always pay 0%

ja.question: What does GDP (Gross Domestic Product) measure?

The value of all goods and services produced in an economy
The amount of cash in circulation
The national debt

ja.question: Why is persistent deflation (falling prices) considered dangerous?

People delay purchases, demand drops, and debts get harder to repay
It always boosts wages
It has no effect on the economy

ja.question: What does “zero” mean in zero-based budgeting?

answers.text: You must spend everything and empty the account
Every available unit has a purpose in the plan, including reserves
Savings must equal zero
Only cash may be used

ja.explanation: This is a planning method, not a requirement to spend everything or empty an account. Hypothetically: PLN 1000 = 800 for essential needs + 100 for required minimum repayments + 100 for a voluntary reserve; unallocated: PLN 0. Repayments are counted once. Update the plan when income varies; no surplus means no duty to save. The plan does not guarantee freedom from unexpected expenses.

ja.question: What can help you understand spending before making or revising a budget?

answers.text: First postpone urgent essential purchases for 30 days
Optionally review your own spending over a suitable period using a method you choose
Everyone must first collect exactly 30 days of data
Borrow money instead of checking spending

ja.explanation: You can start with a day or week of your own notes and extend the period; 30 days is not a mandatory prerequisite. Include less frequent bills and variable income too. Do not postpone urgent essential needs or required minimum repayments while observing. Choose a manageable method and return when you can; you do not need to share data with the app.

ja.question: You have PLN 0 saved for an optional PLN 600 purchase in 6 months. What are 6 equal monthly contributions before purchase, ignoring interest and fees?

answers.text: PLN 600 each month
PLN 100 each month for this planned goal
PLN 0, because reserves guarantee every cost is covered
Borrowing always replaces such a plan

ja.explanation: 600 ÷ 6 = PLN 100 monthly in this hypothetical plan. A sinking fund is for a known future cost; emergency reserves cover unexpected events. Contributions are voluntary, after essential needs and required minimum repayments. With no surplus, change the goal or postpone this optional purchase; update the plan when income varies. There is no guarantee of avoiding debt.

ja.question: What could you optionally do before a non-urgent, non-essential purchase?

answers.text: Always buy immediately and check the cost later
Take a pause you choose and check the need, price and plan
Postpone urgent essential purchases too
Assume every pause guarantees savings

ja.explanation: You can pause and return to the decision at a suitable time. This is an option, not a mandatory 24 hours or a guarantee of savings or a change in desire to buy. Do not postpone urgent essential needs or required minimum repayments. After a break, calmly check the price, available money and priorities; you can revise the decision without pressure.

ja.question: After covering essentials and all required minimum repayments, PLN 20 remains. Which small first step is an optional choice in this example?

answers.text: Save a full month of costs at once as a requirement
Choose e.g. PLN 5; pause if there is no surplus
Borrow PLN 100 to start a reserve
Transfer all income before paying bills

ja.explanation: Example budget: PLN 1,200 income − PLN 1,080 essentials − PLN 100 required minimums = PLN 20 surplus, with no other costs or fees. An optional PLN 5 leaves PLN 15; no transfer is required. Adapt the goal to circumstances without requiring a full month at the start. Without surplus, pause; do not borrow to save.

Risk and return are unrelated
Lower risk always means higher return

Borrow money to buy more

ja.question: 投資における「分散」とは？

ja.question: 「借金の雪崩（アバランチ）」戦略とは？

借金が増えるまで放っておく

ja.question: インフレが5%で銀行の金利が2%のとき、貯蓄の実質リターンは？
ja.explanation: 実質リターン＝名目金利−インフレ率＝2%−5%＝−3%。金利2%の預金でも、お金は購買力を失っています。

ja.question: 低い手数料で市場の指数に自動的に連動するファンドは？

インデックスファンド／ETF
ベンチャーキャピタルファンド
年金ファンド

ja.question: ドルコスト平均法（DCA）とは？

answers.text: 市場の底で全部買う
価格が下がったら全部売る
価格に関係なく、一定の間隔で一定額を投資する
貯蓄をすべて米ドルに換える

ja.explanation: ドルコスト平均法は、価格に関係なく毎月同じ金額を投資する方法です。安いときに多く、高いときに少なく買うことになり、投資から感情を取り除けます。

ja.question: 「72の法則」とは？

収入の72%を貯蓄する
年金を最大にするため72歳で引退する

ja.question: ETFとは？

電子送金の手数料
上場投資信託：株のように取引される資産のバスケット
政府の緊急資金

ja.question: 良い緊急資金の特徴ではないものはどれ？

普段使う口座と分けている

ja.question: 年金・老後用口座の主な目的は？

高リスク資産で投機する
緊急用の現金を置いておく

ja.question: OECDのデータによると、複利を正しく理解しているポーランド人は何%？

ja.question: ポーランド人のほぼ半数が、お金に人生を支配されていると答えています。すすめられる考え方の転換は？

ja.question: OECDによると、金融姿勢の最低目標スコアに達しているポーランド人は26.9%だけです。「金融姿勢」は何を測る？

hi.question: What is 'net worth'?

Total assets minus total liabilities
How much cash you have in your wallet
Your credit score

hi.question: What is 'lifestyle inflation'?

Prices rising faster than salaries
Choosing more discretionary spending as your income rises
Inflating your lifestyle on your resume

hi.question: What does 'pay yourself first' mean?

Plan affordable savings after reserving money for essentials and required minimum payments
Increase your own salary first

hi.question: With PLN 4,000 take-home income, what is the illustrative 20% bucket?

answers.text: PLN 800

hi.question: Which checklist is most complete when comparing savings accounts in Poland?

Rates and conditions, fees, access, and deposit protection
Whether the account guarantees an inflation-beating return
Whether your deposit is automatically invested in stocks

hi.question: You invest PLN 100 twice, at PLN 10 then PLN 20 per unit. What do you buy?

A guaranteed profit

hi.question: For one year, assumed nominal return is 2% and inflation 5%, with no fees, tax or cash flows. What is real return?

hi.question: Assume a fixed 6% nominal rate, annual compounding and no fees, tax or cash flows. What does Rule of 72 estimate?

hi.question: Someone says an investment will always beat inflation. Which response is justified?

hi.question: After essentials and required minimums, PLN 100 remains. A PLN 1,000 debt charges 20% and a PLN 500 debt 10% annually; fixed rates, no fees, penalties or arrears. Where does avalanche direct the extra?

hi.question: Which statement distinguishes BIK repayment history from repayment capacity in Poland?

hi.question: You sell a fixed-cash-flow bond before maturity. Its required market yield rises, other factors unchanged. What happens to its price?

The coupon automatically rises
Principal at maturity automatically falls

hi.explanation: For the same fixed cash flows, a higher required yield means a lower secondary-market price. This does not automatically change the coupon or contractual principal at maturity. Sale price, redemption terms and default risk are distinct; this is not a rule for every bond.

hi.question: Which decision conflicts with a readily accessible reserve with low volatility?

answers.text: Check access timing
Check fees and protection scope
Put the entire reserve in volatile shares
Distinguish reserves from planned spending

hi.explanation: An entire reserve in volatile shares may lose value when needed. Check access, fees and terms; lower risk does not mean no losses or costs. Deposit protection depends on the institution and product, and does not cover every investment. This is not a provider choice.

hi.question: Example: PLN 1,000 income, PLN 900 essentials, PLN 80 required minimums, no other costs or fees. Which small start fits these conditions?

answers.text: Transfer PLN 100 from a PLN 20 surplus
Optionally save PLN 10, leaving PLN 10
Borrow to save
Treat one month of costs as a required first threshold

hi.explanation: 1,000 − 900 − 80 = PLN 20. An optional PLN 10 fits the surplus and leaves PLN 10; no transfer is required. At PLN 980 income, surplus is PLN 0. One month of expenses is not a required first goal; without funds, pause the transfer and do not borrow to save.

hi.question: What is compound interest when credited interest stays in the balance?

answers.text: Interest only on the initial amount
An early withdrawal fee
Interest on principal and retained earlier interest
A certain profit from every investment

hi.explanation: In a hypothetical model, PLN 1,000 at a constant 5% a year with annual compounding becomes PLN 1,050, then PLN 1,102.50. Interest stays; there are no contributions, withdrawals, fees or tax, and inflation is ignored. The extra PLN 2.50 is interest on the first PLN 50 of interest. This is a nominal model, not an offer or guaranteed investment profit.

hi.question: What is the purpose of diversification, without guaranteeing no losses?

answers.text: Putting everything into one company
Spreading investments to reduce concentration risk
Ensuring a profit regardless of the market
Changing the portfolio weekly to ensure a profit

hi.explanation: Different investments can reduce dependence on one issuer or sector. Multiple holdings may still share risks and fall together. Diversification does not guarantee profit or remove the risk of market losses.

hi.question: What defines an index fund?

answers.text: Always having zero costs
An objective of tracking a specified index
Every ETF being an index fund
A guaranteed return above the market

hi.explanation: An index fund seeks to track a specified index. Costs and tracking error can create differences in returns. Not every index fund is cheaper; check actual costs and risks. An ETF may track an index or be actively managed. The name does not promise market outperformance.

hi.question: What does ETF mean?

answers.text: An account with guaranteed interest
A bank transfer fee
A fund whose shares trade on an exchange
A fund that always tracks a broad index

hi.explanation: An ETF is an exchange-traded fund. It may follow an index or an active strategy and hold a narrow set of investments. An ETF alone does not ensure broad diversification or protect capital. Check holdings, risks, fees and buying and selling costs; losses are possible.

hi.question: What belongs in an investment plan instead of assuming time alone guarantees profit?

answers.text: The date of a certain market bottom
Goals, horizon, reserves, acceptable losses and costs
Always selling after a 10% drop
Always holding every investment

hi.explanation: A long horizon alone does not guarantee profit. A plan depends on goals, when money is needed, reserves, risk and costs; it can be reassessed when circumstances change. This is not an always-hold or sell-after-a-set-drop rule. Essentials and required minimums come first, and without surplus it is acceptable not to invest.

hi.question: What is the purpose of planning finances for retirement?

answers.text: Certainty of maintaining every current income
Preparing resources for future needs after work changes or ends
Replacing emergency reserves with a risky investment
Doubling money simply by opening an account

hi.explanation: A plan compares future needs and possible sources of funds; it does not guarantee maintaining current income. Emergency reserves have a separate role. Outcomes depend on contributions, conditions, costs and risk, among other factors. Essentials, required minimum repayments and reserves come first; without surplus, start with a free planning exercise, without buying anything or opening an account.

hi.question: Model: PLN 1,000 once, a constant 5% a year, annual compounding, interest retained. No later contributions, withdrawals, fees or tax; inflation ignored. What is the nominal balance after 2 years?
hi.explanation: In this hypothetical model, 1,000 × 1.05 × 1.05 = PLN 1,102.50. After year one the balance is PLN 1,050; the second interest payment is PLN 52.50. The positive result comes from the assumed constant rate, not time alone. More periods allow more compounding here, but actual outcomes can differ and losses are possible. This is not a pension forecast or a recommendation to contribute.

hi.question: What can a survey percentage of correct answers about compound interest in Poland tell us?

answers.text: Everyone answering incorrectly will fall into debt
Knowledge alone guarantees a high pension
It is a result of specific questions, sample, year and scoring
That percentage describes all financial behaviour

hi.explanation: Check the year, surveyed population, questions and scoring method. A knowledge result is not the same as behaviour or financial circumstances. A statistical association alone does not prove that lacking this knowledge directly causes debt or low retirement savings.

hi.question: Does a survey percentage of stated trust establish that a particular institution is safe?

answers.text: Yes, if it has many customers
Yes, every higher percentage means no risk
Yes, if the result is older
No; a survey does not replace checking the institution

hi.explanation: Check the date, sample and exact wording, including whether the question concerns institutions or their employees. Stated trust does not certify a particular institution or product as safe. A percentage alone also does not prove a cause of savings or wealth.

hi.question: How should a gap to the maximum financial-literacy survey score be interpreted?

answers.text: As a certain amount of lost savings
As a point gap dependent on questions and scoring
As a future investment return
As proof that the respondent is to blame

hi.explanation: Check the year, sample, instrument version and scoring key. A historical result does not automatically describe the current population. A point gap does not measure lost wealth and alone proves neither behaviour nor causes of financial difficulties.

hi.question: What should be established before comparing PPK and PPE participation percentages?

answers.text: Only the highest percentage
That both names mean the same programme
The separate programme, date and group used for each percentage
That non-participation proves a lack of knowledge

hi.explanation: PPK and PPE are separate arrangements. Identify the programme, date, surveyed group and denominator; do not combine percentages without a stated method. Participation statistics alone explain neither why people decide nor whether a lack of compound-interest knowledge caused that decision.

hi.question: Which set most fully describes financial well-being in the CFPB framework?

answers.text: Only income level
Day-to-day finances, shock absorption, goals and freedom of choice
Only a financial quiz score
The number of financial products owned

hi.explanation: The CFPB framework covers a sense of control over current finances, capacity to handle shocks, progress towards goals and freedom of choice. It is a descriptive framework, not a guarantee after mastering three tasks. Resources, circumstances and personal perceptions also matter; not everything depends on individual choices.

hi.question: What best describes financial resilience?

answers.text: A guaranteed million in savings
An absolute absence of any debt
The capacity to handle a financial shock and rebuild one’s situation
Merely having an insurance policy

hi.explanation: Income, resources, obligations, available support and the size of a shock matter, not just knowledge or mindset. A reserve may help but guarantees no coverage of every expense. Choose contributions voluntarily after essential needs and required minimum repayments; without a surplus, pause contributions.

hi.question: Exercise: PLN 1000 debt, a hypothetical fixed 10% per period added to the debt. For 2 periods there are no repayments, fees or new borrowing. What is the balance?

answers.text: PLN 1000
PLN 1210
PLN 1200
PLN 2000

hi.explanation: 1000 × 1.10 × 1.10 = PLN 1210. This is an assumed model, not an offer or a rule for every contract. Actual cost depends on terms and repayments. Debt difficulties can also involve lost income, unexpected costs and fees. A quiz establishes neither the cause of difficulties nor a person’s blame.

hi.question: What is the main purpose of life insurance?

answers.text: To get rich when someone dies
To replace income for dependents if the primary earner dies
To save on taxes
To invest in the stock market safely

hi.explanation: Life insurance protects dependents by replacing the primary earner's income if they die prematurely.

hi.question: What is the recommended approach to finances for couples?

answers.text: One partner handles all finances, the other doesn't need to know
Both partners should understand the full financial picture and plan together
Keep all finances 100% separate — never share anything
Whoever earns more controls all decisions

hi.explanation: Financial transparency and joint planning between partners leads to better decisions and fewer conflicts.

hi.question: What is the most effective way to teach kids about money?

answers.text: Give them pocket money with no conditions
Let them observe — never discuss money with children
Give pocket money with saving rules (e.g. save 20%, spend 60%, give 20%)
Wait until they're 18 to discuss finances

hi.explanation: Pocket money with saving/spending rules gives kids real financial decisions at low cost.

hi.question: What inflation rate has the National Bank of Poland (NBP) targeted since 2004?

answers.text: 0% — prices should never rise
2.5% with a ±1 percentage point band
5% to encourage spending
Whatever the government sets each year

hi.explanation: Since 2004 the NBP's target is 2.5% (±1 percentage point), measured by the annual change in the CPI.

hi.question: Why do central banks aim for low, positive inflation (~2–2.5%) instead of 0%?

answers.text: To make the currency worthless faster
A small, stable buffer supports growth and avoids dangerous deflation
Because higher prices are always good
To increase government tax revenue only

hi.explanation: A low, stable target avoids deflation (which can stall an economy) and keeps inflation predictable.

hi.question: What is a central bank's main tool for steering inflation?

answers.text: Printing more banknotes for citizens
Setting benchmark interest rates
Fixing the price of bread
Banning imports

hi.explanation: Central banks mainly use benchmark interest rates to influence borrowing, demand and ultimately inflation.

hi.question: When a central bank raises interest rates, what typically happens?

answers.text: Borrowing gets cheaper and spending jumps
Borrowing gets more expensive, cooling demand and inflation
Nothing changes for households
Savings accounts always pay 0%

hi.explanation: Rate hikes raise the cost of borrowing, which cools spending and helps bring inflation down.

hi.question: What does GDP (Gross Domestic Product) measure?

answers.text: The total savings of all citizens
The value of all goods and services produced in an economy
The amount of cash in circulation
The national debt

hi.explanation: GDP = the total market value of goods and services produced in a country over a period.

hi.question: Why is persistent deflation (falling prices) considered dangerous?

answers.text: It makes everyone richer with no downside
People delay purchases, demand drops, and debts get harder to repay
It always boosts wages
It has no effect on the economy

hi.explanation: Deflation pushes people to delay spending and makes existing debt heavier in real terms — a dangerous loop.

hi.question: What does “zero” mean in zero-based budgeting?

answers.text: You must spend everything and empty the account
Every available unit has a purpose in the plan, including reserves
Savings must equal zero
Only cash may be used

hi.explanation: This is a planning method, not a requirement to spend everything or empty an account. Hypothetically: PLN 1000 = 800 for essential needs + 100 for required minimum repayments + 100 for a voluntary reserve; unallocated: PLN 0. Repayments are counted once. Update the plan when income varies; no surplus means no duty to save. The plan does not guarantee freedom from unexpected expenses.

hi.question: What can help you understand spending before making or revising a budget?

answers.text: First postpone urgent essential purchases for 30 days
Optionally review your own spending over a suitable period using a method you choose
Everyone must first collect exactly 30 days of data
Borrow money instead of checking spending

hi.explanation: You can start with a day or week of your own notes and extend the period; 30 days is not a mandatory prerequisite. Include less frequent bills and variable income too. Do not postpone urgent essential needs or required minimum repayments while observing. Choose a manageable method and return when you can; you do not need to share data with the app.

hi.question: You have PLN 0 saved for an optional PLN 600 purchase in 6 months. What are 6 equal monthly contributions before purchase, ignoring interest and fees?

answers.text: PLN 600 each month
PLN 100 each month for this planned goal
PLN 0, because reserves guarantee every cost is covered
Borrowing always replaces such a plan

hi.explanation: 600 ÷ 6 = PLN 100 monthly in this hypothetical plan. A sinking fund is for a known future cost; emergency reserves cover unexpected events. Contributions are voluntary, after essential needs and required minimum repayments. With no surplus, change the goal or postpone this optional purchase; update the plan when income varies. There is no guarantee of avoiding debt.

hi.question: What could you optionally do before a non-urgent, non-essential purchase?

answers.text: Always buy immediately and check the cost later
Take a pause you choose and check the need, price and plan
Postpone urgent essential purchases too
Assume every pause guarantees savings

hi.explanation: You can pause and return to the decision at a suitable time. This is an option, not a mandatory 24 hours or a guarantee of savings or a change in desire to buy. Do not postpone urgent essential needs or required minimum repayments. After a break, calmly check the price, available money and priorities; you can revise the decision without pressure.

hi.question: After covering essentials and all required minimum repayments, PLN 20 remains. Which small first step is an optional choice in this example?

answers.text: Save a full month of costs at once as a requirement
Choose e.g. PLN 5; pause if there is no surplus
Borrow PLN 100 to start a reserve
Transfer all income before paying bills

hi.explanation: Example budget: PLN 1,200 income − PLN 1,080 essentials − PLN 100 required minimums = PLN 20 surplus, with no other costs or fees. An optional PLN 5 leaves PLN 15; no transfer is required. Adapt the goal to circumstances without requiring a full month at the start. Without surplus, pause; do not borrow to save.

hi.question: In Poland, up to what amount are bank deposits guaranteed by the BFG?

answers.text: There is no deposit guarantee
The PLN equivalent of €100,000 per depositor, per bank
Exactly 10,000 PLN total
Unlimited, always 100%

hi.explanation: Poland's BFG guarantees deposits up to the PLN equivalent of €100,000 per depositor in each bank.

hi.question: What is the general relationship between risk and expected return?

answers.text: Higher expected returns generally come with higher risk
High returns are guaranteed with zero risk
Risk and return are unrelated
Lower risk always means higher return

hi.explanation: Higher potential return generally requires taking on more risk. Be sceptical of 'high return, no risk' offers.

hi.question: How should beginners treat highly speculative assets like crypto?

answers.text: Put all savings in for maximum gains
Limit to a small share you could afford to lose entirely
Borrow money to buy more
Treat it as a safe emergency fund

hi.explanation: Keep speculative assets to a small portion of your portfolio, and only money you can afford to lose completely.

hi.question: What's the key tax difference between Poland's IKE and IKZE accounts?

answers.text: They are identical in every way
IKE: tax-free gains on a qualifying withdrawal; IKZE: deduct contributions now, pay a 10% flat tax on withdrawal
Both are taxed at 19% every year
Neither offers any tax benefit

hi.explanation: IKE = tax-free growth on qualifying withdrawal. IKZE = deduct contributions today, 10% flat tax when you withdraw.

hi.question: In Poland's PPK, what does the employer add on top of the employee's 2% basic contribution?

answers.text: Nothing — only the employee pays
A basic 1.5% of salary (plus an optional extra up to 2.5%)
A flat 100 PLN regardless of salary
10% of salary

hi.explanation: PPK: employee 2% basic, employer adds 1.5% basic (up to +2.5% extra). The employer match is free retirement money.

hi.question: What state incentives does Poland's PPK give participants?

answers.text: No state support at all
A 250 PLN welcome payment and a 240 PLN annual bonus
A 50,000 PLN lump sum
Free shares in the employer

hi.explanation: PPK state support: a one-off 250 PLN welcome payment and a 240 PLN annual bonus for participants.

hi.question: What do deposit guarantee schemes (BFG, FDIC, EU DGS, FGC) actually protect?

answers.text: All investments including stocks and crypto
Bank deposits — not stocks, funds, pensions or crypto
Only cash kept at home
Your salary if you lose your job

hi.explanation: These schemes protect bank deposits only. Stocks, funds, pensions and crypto fall outside them.

hi.question: In the United States, how much does the FDIC insure per depositor, per bank?

answers.text: $250,000 (per ownership category)
Unlimited
There is no deposit insurance in the US

hi.explanation: US FDIC coverage is $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each ownership category.

hi.question: Across the EU (incl. Poland, Spain, France), bank deposits are guaranteed up to…

answers.text: €1,000 per country
€100,000 per depositor, per bank (or local-currency equivalent)
Nothing is guaranteed in the EU

hi.explanation: EU rules harmonise deposit protection at €100,000 per depositor, per bank.

hi.question: With a US 401(k) that offers an employer match, what's the smartest first move?

answers.text: Skip it — matches are a trick
Contribute at least enough to get the full employer match (free money)
Only contribute after age 60
Put it all into a single company stock

hi.explanation: Always contribute enough to capture the full employer match — it's free money you can't get any other way.

hi.question: What do a UK ISA, a Japanese NISA and a Polish IKE have in common?

answers.text: They guarantee a fixed 10% return
They are tax-advantaged accounts that shelter investment growth
They are types of credit card
They are only for millionaires

hi.explanation: ISA (UK), NISA (Japan) and IKE (Poland) are tax-advantaged accounts that shelter investment gains.

hi.question: What inflation target does India's central bank (RBI) aim for?

answers.text: 4% with a ±2 percentage point tolerance band
It has no target

hi.explanation: India's RBI targets 4% inflation with a tolerance band of ±2 percentage points (2–6%).

hi.question: 50/30/20 बजट नियम क्या है?
hi.explanation: 50% ज़रूरतों (किराया, खाना) के लिए, 30% चाहतों (मनोरंजन) के लिए और 20% बचत व कर्ज़ चुकाने के लिए। सरल और कारगर।

hi.question: चक्रवृद्धि ब्याज क्या है?

answers.text: सिर्फ़ मूल रकम पर मिलने वाला ब्याज
समय से पहले निकासी पर बैंक शुल्क
मूलधन और पहले मिले ब्याज दोनों पर मिलने वाला ब्याज
वह ब्याज जो आप सिर्फ़ क्रेडिट कार्ड पर चुकाते हैं

hi.explanation: चक्रवृद्धि ब्याज का मतलब है कि आपके ब्याज पर भी ब्याज मिलता है; समय के साथ इससे तेज़ी से बढ़ोतरी होती है। कहा जाता है कि आइंस्टीन ने इसे दुनिया का आठवां अजूबा कहा था।

hi.question: निवेश में 'विविधीकरण' का क्या मतलब है?

answers.text: अपना सारा पैसा एक मज़बूत शेयर में लगाना
जोखिम घटाने के लिए निवेश को अलग-अलग एसेट में फैलाना
सिर्फ़ सरकारी बॉन्ड में निवेश करना
हर हफ़्ते अपना पोर्टफ़ोलियो बदलना

hi.explanation: सारे अंडे एक ही टोकरी में न रखें। विविधीकरण इस जोखिम को घटाता है कि एक खराब निवेश आपका पूरा पोर्टफ़ोलियो बिगाड़ दे।

hi.question: 'डेट एवलांच' रणनीति क्या है?

answers.text: पुराने लोन चुकाने के लिए नए लोन लेना
ब्याज दर देखे बिना सबसे छोटे कर्ज़ पहले चुकाना
कुल ब्याज कम करने के लिए सबसे ऊंचे ब्याज वाले कर्ज़ पहले चुकाना
कर्ज़ को बढ़ने तक अनदेखा करना

hi.explanation: डेट एवलांच = सबसे ऊंची ब्याज दर पर पहले वार करें। गणित के हिसाब से यह सबसे ज़्यादा पैसा बचाता है। इसके उलट 'डेट स्नोबॉल' में हौसले के लिए सबसे छोटे बकाये पहले चुकाए जाते हैं।

hi.question: अगर महंगाई 5% है और बैंक 2% देता है, तो आपकी बचत का असली रिटर्न क्या है?
hi.explanation: असली रिटर्न = नाममात्र दर − महंगाई = 2% − 5% = −3%। 2% वाले बचत खाते में भी आपका पैसा क्रय शक्ति खो रहा है।

hi.question: किस तरह का फंड कम शुल्क पर बाज़ार के इंडेक्स को अपने आप ट्रैक करता है?

answers.text: हेज फंड
इंडेक्स फंड / ETF
वेंचर कैपिटल फंड
पेंशन फंड

hi.explanation: इंडेक्स फंड और ETF बाज़ार के किसी इंडेक्स (जैसे S&P 500) को निष्क्रिय रूप से ट्रैक करते हैं। इनका शुल्क बहुत कम होता है और ये ऐतिहासिक रूप से ज़्यादातर सक्रिय फंडों से बेहतर रहे हैं।

hi.question: नियमित निवेश (SIP/DCA) क्या है?

answers.text: बाज़ार के सबसे निचले स्तर पर सब खरीद लेना
कीमतें गिरने पर सब बेच देना
कीमत चाहे जो हो, नियमित अंतराल पर तय रकम निवेश करना
सारी बचत को डॉलर में बदल देना

hi.explanation: DCA का मतलब है कीमत चाहे जो हो, हर महीने वही तय रकम निवेश करना। कीमतें कम होने पर आप ज़्यादा और ऊंची होने पर कम खरीदते हैं, जिससे निवेश से भावनाएं हट जाती हैं।

hi.question: '72 का नियम' क्या है?

answers.text: किसी भी कर्ज़ को चुकाने में 72 महीने लगते हैं
72 को सालाना रिटर्न से भाग दें और जानें कि पैसा कितने साल में दोगुना होगा
अपनी आय का 72% बचाएं
ज़्यादा पेंशन के लिए 72 की उम्र में रिटायर हों

hi.explanation: 72 ÷ सालाना रिटर्न % = पैसा दोगुना होने के साल। 8% पर पैसा लगभग 9 साल में दोगुना होता है, 6% पर लगभग 12 साल में। झटपट मन में हिसाब लगाने का तरीका।

hi.question: ETF क्या है?

answers.text: ज़्यादा ब्याज वाला बचत खाता
इलेक्ट्रॉनिक ट्रांसफ़र शुल्क
एक्सचेंज-ट्रेडेड फंड: एसेट की टोकरी जो शेयर की तरह खरीदी-बेची जाती है
सरकारी आपातकालीन फंड

hi.explanation: ETF कई एसेट (शेयर, बॉन्ड, कमोडिटी) को एक ही ट्रेड होने वाले साधन में जोड़ते हैं। ये म्यूचुअल फंड के विविधीकरण को शेयर के लचीलेपन के साथ जोड़ते हैं।

hi.question: इनमें से कौन सी बात अच्छे आपातकालीन फंड की खासियत नहीं है?

answers.text: आसानी से उपलब्ध (लिक्विड)
3–6 महीने के खर्च कवर करता है
अधिकतम बढ़त के लिए ऊंचे जोखिम वाले शेयरों में लगा हुआ
रोज़मर्रा के खर्च वाले खाते से अलग रखा गया

hi.explanation: आपातकालीन फंड लिक्विड और सुरक्षित होना चाहिए, अस्थिर एसेट में लगा हुआ नहीं। इसका मकसद बढ़ना नहीं, आपात स्थिति में उपलब्ध रहना है।

hi.question: ब्याज दरें बढ़ने पर बॉन्ड की कीमतों का क्या होता है?

answers.text: बॉन्ड की कीमतें बढ़ती हैं
बॉन्ड की कीमतें गिरती हैं
कोई बदलाव नहीं
बॉन्ड की कीमतें दोगुनी हो जाती हैं

hi.explanation: बॉन्ड और ब्याज दरें उलटी दिशा में चलते हैं। दरें बढ़ने पर कम दर वाले मौजूदा बॉन्ड कम आकर्षक हो जाते हैं, इसलिए उनकी बाज़ार कीमत गिरती है।

hi.question: 'जीवनशैली की महंगाई' क्या है?

answers.text: सरकार का न्यूनतम वेतन बढ़ाना
कीमतों का वेतन से तेज़ बढ़ना
कमाई बढ़ने के साथ ज़्यादा खर्च करना और बचत को वैसा ही छोड़ देना
अपने रेज़्यूमे में जीवनशैली को बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर दिखाना

hi.explanation: जीवनशैली की महंगाई का मतलब है कि हर वेतन वृद्धि नए खर्चों में खप जाती है। इलाज: अतिरिक्त आय की आदत पड़ने से पहले ही वृद्धि को बचा लें।

hi.question: पेंशन/रिटायरमेंट खाते का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है?

answers.text: छुट्टियों का खर्च उठाना
दशकों की चक्रवृद्धि से, काम छोड़ने पर आय की जगह लेना
ऊंचे जोखिम वाले एसेट पर सट्टा लगाना
आपातकालीन नकदी रखना

hi.explanation: रिटायरमेंट खाते लंबी अवधि के साधन हैं। योगदान दशकों तक कर लाभ के साथ बढ़ते हैं। समय आपकी सबसे बड़ी संपत्ति है: 35 की जगह 25 में शुरू करने से अंतिम रकम दोगुनी हो सकती है।

hi.question: 'नेट वर्थ' का क्या मतलब है?

answers.text: टैक्स के बाद आपका मासिक वेतन
कुल संपत्ति में से कुल देनदारियां घटाकर
आपके बटुए में कितनी नकदी है
आपका क्रेडिट स्कोर

hi.explanation: नेट वर्थ = जो कुछ आपके पास है (संपत्ति) उसमें से जो कुछ आप पर बकाया है (देनदारियां) घटाकर। सकारात्मक और बढ़ती नेट वर्थ वित्तीय सेहत का असली पैमाना है, अकेली आय से ज़्यादा सार्थक।

hi.question: OECD के आंकड़ों के अनुसार, कितने प्रतिशत पोलिश लोग चक्रवृद्धि ब्याज को सही समझते हैं?

answers.text: लगभग 75%
लगभग 50%
लगभग 33%
लगभग 10%

hi.explanation: व्यवहार में हर 3 में से सिर्फ़ 1 पोलिश व्यक्ति चक्रवृद्धि ब्याज समझता है। यह सबसे बड़ी जानकारी की कमी है: इससे कर्ज़ का चक्र बनता है और यही बताता है कि सिर्फ़ 47% कर्मचारी स्वैच्छिक PPK/PPE पेंशन योजनाओं से क्यों जुड़ते हैं।

hi.question: 2022 में कितने प्रतिशत पोलिश लोग बचत के लिए वित्तीय संस्थानों पर भरोसा करते थे?
hi.explanation: 2022 में सिर्फ़ 15% पोलिश लोग वित्तीय संस्थानों पर भरोसा करते थे, और 2021 में यह घटकर सिर्फ़ 6% रह गया था। भरोसे की यह कमी वित्तीय भागीदारी और लंबी अवधि में संपत्ति बनाने की बड़ी बाधा है।

hi.question: OECD वित्तीय दक्षता में पोलैंड को 13/21 मिले। छूटे हुए अंक क्या दर्शाते हैं?

answers.text: कुछ खास नहीं: 13/21 बहुत अच्छा है
संपत्ति बनाने के खोए हुए अवसर और वित्तीय तैयारी की कमी
OECD परीक्षण में भाषा की बाधा
बैंक खातों की कम संख्या

hi.explanation: 13/21 का स्कोर पोलैंड को बीच में रखता है। छूटे हुए 8 अंक ठोस खोए हुए अवसर हैं: पूंजी बाज़ार का कम प्रभावी उपयोग, आपातकालीन फंड की कम दर और आर्थिक झटकों के प्रति ज़्यादा असुरक्षा।

hi.question: लगभग आधे पोलिश लोग कहते हैं कि उनका पैसा उनकी ज़िंदगी चलाता है। सोच में कौन सा बदलाव सुझाया जाता है?

answers.text: किसी भी कीमत पर ज़्यादा पैसा कमाना
तनाव घटाने के लिए पैसे के बारे में सोचना टालना
अपने नियंत्रण का एहसास वापस पाना: पैसे को तनाव का कारण नहीं, एक साधन मानना
सब कुछ वित्तीय सलाहकार पर छोड़ देना

hi.explanation: जब लोगों को लगता है कि उनके हाथ में कुछ नहीं है, तब अल्पकालिक सोच एक मनोवैज्ञानिक बचाव होती है। वित्तीय शिक्षा को नियंत्रण का यह एहसास लौटाना चाहिए और पैसे को तनाव के कारण से सशक्तीकरण के साधन में बदलना चाहिए।

hi.question: कौन सी पोलिश अवधारणा आपातकालीन वित्तीय कुशन को दर्शाती है?

answers.text: Kapitał własny
Poduszka finansowa
Rezerwa walutowa
Dywidenda bezpieczeństwa

hi.explanation: 'Poduszka finansowa' (वित्तीय तकिया) आपातकालीन फंड के लिए पोलिश शब्द है। यह वित्तीय खुशहाली का मुख्य हिस्सा है: ऊंचे ब्याज पर उधार लिए बिना अचानक आए झटकों को संभालने का सुरक्षा कवच।

hi.question: OECD ने पाया कि सिर्फ़ 26.9% पोलिश लोग न्यूनतम वित्तीय दृष्टिकोण स्कोर तक पहुंचते हैं। 'वित्तीय दृष्टिकोण' क्या मापता है?

answers.text: किसी के पास कितने वित्तीय उत्पाद हैं
आय का स्तर और बचत की दर
कोई भविष्य की योजना बनाता है या सिर्फ़ आज के लिए जीता है
बैंकों पर भरोसे का स्तर

hi.explanation: वित्तीय दृष्टिकोण सिर्फ़ वर्तमान की सोच के मुकाबले भविष्य की योजना की ओर झुकाव मापता है। पोलैंड का 26.9% OECD औसत का लगभग आधा है और अल्पकालिक वित्तीय सोच की व्यापक संस्कृति को दर्शाता है।

pt-BR.question: O que significa inflação?

answers.text: O dinheiro compra mais com o tempo
O dinheiro perde poder de compra com o tempo
Bancos dão dinheiro de graça
Os preços sempre caem

pt-BR.explanation: Inflação significa que a mesma quantia compra menos com o tempo.

pt-BR.question: Quantos meses de despesas um fundo de emergência deve cobrir?

answers.text: 1 semana
1 mês
3 a 6 meses
10 anos
